Three steps, deliberately separate because their cost differs by orders of magnitude: A the map XML one request every place in the database, with coordinates B the place pages 1–2 per place the ensembles of a place and their years C the ensemble pages 1 per ensemble an ensemble's own chronicle and active decades Step A — enumeration ajax/map2.php?zoom=12&nex=…&ney=…&swx=…&swy=… returns one XML document of <location> elements (id, name, lat, lng, typ, typnazev, alive) whose CDATA body names the kraj and the okres with their own geo ids. Below zoom ~8 the endpoint returns kraj aggregates instead, so the zoom is fixed high. The XML carries no dates . Step B — dates, and the view switch that decides what a page says By default the site shows only ensembles active today and shortened records. The historical view is a PHP-session switch : the page's own buttons call ajax/prepinac.php?co=rozsah&val=1 (Historie) and …?co=delka&val=1 (Úplné záznamy) and reload. A scraper that forgets this gets a well-formed page listing one ensemble where there are thirteen — a silent error, not a loud one. So: one session is kept for the whole run and both switches are set first; a canary is then fetched live: geo id 936, Uhlířské Janovice, must list Beseda (od 1873 do 1908) , or the run stops ( HistoryViewError ); every page is checked before it is cached — each carries the switch buttons with the active one marked, so a session that expired mid-run is caught on the page where it happened ( view_state ), re-established once, and otherwise fatal. Nothing is written to the cache unless it was served in the historical, full view. Per place, two pages are available: main.php?data=geo&id={geo_id} the place entry: type, okres, 'První zpráva', a chronicle, bibliography, archive citations — and, under 'Související Soubory', the ensembles with their years index.php?data=soubor&list=soubor11&id={geo_id} the ensemble list alone The place page's block is a superset: it prints each ensemble as Place: Name (span) and also lists the ensembles filed under other places — a town's parts, a touring group's other homes. Only the rows filed under the page's own heading are this place's ( parse_place_ensembles ). Read that way the two pages agree — on all 91 places of the 2026-10-12 pilot for which both were fetched ( compare_sources re-checks it on whatever is cached) — so the default is pages=("geo",) , one request per place, and pages=("geo", "list") is there for a cross-check. Step C — the ensemble pages index.php?data=soubor&id={ensemble_id} is the ensemble's own entry, and it says what the place page does not: Působení , the decades in which the ensemble is recorded active ( 188x, 189x, 190x ), its own founding and last-report fields, its own chronicle — the plays, venues and officers of this ensemble, not of the place — with bibliography and archive citations, and the people tied to it. It is served under the same session switches as the place pages and checked the same way before it is cached. At ~1.5 s a request the 34,154 ensembles are a day's run, so step C is meant for a selection: by default the ensembles that select_ensemble_ids cannot rule out as starting before 1914 (certainly before, or a 191x / 19xx start that straddles it). What the dates are — and are not První zpráva is the first surviving report of theatre in the place, not a founding date. An ensemble's span is printed as (od 1873 do 1908) ; the years may be fuzzy ( 191x , 19xx ) or the span open-ended ( (od 1936) ). A fuzzy year is kept as its decade or century with a precision flag and its printed form beside it — it is never coerced to a year ( parse_year_token ). Politeness The site is a small public-sector database behind Cloudflare; the client is built so that it cannot hurt it. Sequential, one connection , never parallel. At least one second between requests — delay below MIN_DELAY is refused, the default is 1.5 s — and the pause stretches with the server's own response time (twice the last response time, capped), so a slow server is given room. Every response is cached on disk and never requested twice; a re-run costs only the canary. Backs off on 429/5xx (honouring Retry-After ), gives up after a run of consecutive failures ( ServerUnhealthyError ) rather than hammering a server that is down, and stops at once on a Cloudflare challenge ( BlockedError ) — bot protection is never worked around. Rests batch_pause seconds every batch_size requests. The User-Agent names this script and its version — a script, not a browser — and nothing about who runs it. The site publishes no robots.txt (404 on 2026-10-12) and its pages carry <meta name="robots" content="ALL,FOLLOW"> . Source and citation Databáze českého amatérského divadla [online]. Praha: NIK – Národní institut pro kulturu (dříve NIPOS), 2005–2026. https://www.amaterskedivadlo.cz Cite with the retrieval date written to SOURCE.txt in the output directory, and cite an individual place as its heading plus main.php?data=geo&id={geo_id} (an ensemble as its name plus index.php?data=soubor&id={ensemble_id} ). The database grew out of Místopis českého amatérského divadla I–II (Praha: IPOS-ARTAMA, 2001–2002), which its entries cite; that is the print source to cite beside it. All rights reserved by NIK (NIPOS); scraping rests on the same basis as the project's other sources — §90 zákon č. 121/2000 Sb. (scientific research). The raw cache stays under the gitignored data/ tree and is not redistributed; only facts (names, places, years) are extracted. českého amatérského divadla* (DbČAD), the encyclopedic database of Czech amateur theatre kept by NIK – Národní institut pro kulturu (formerly NIPOS), for one question: is the date at which amateur theatre is first documented in a place usable as a settlement-level, dated measure of pre-1914 Czech associational life? Three steps, deliberately separate because their cost differs by orders of magnitude: A the map XML one request every place in the database, with coordinates B the place pages 1–2 per place the ensembles of a place and their years C the ensemble pages 1 per ensemble an ensemble's own chronicle and active decades Step A — enumeration -------------------- ``ajax/map2.php?zoom=12&nex=…&ney=…&swx=…&swy=…`` returns one XML document of ```` elements (id, name, lat, lng, typ, typnazev, alive) whose CDATA body names the kraj and the okres with their own geo ids. Below zoom ~8 the endpoint returns kraj aggregates instead, so the zoom is fixed high. The XML carries **no dates**. Step B — dates, and the view switch that decides what a page says ----------------------------------------------------------------- By default the site shows only ensembles active *today* and shortened records. The historical view is a **PHP-session switch**: the page's own buttons call ``ajax/prepinac.php?co=rozsah&val=1`` (Historie) and ``…?co=delka&val=1`` (Úplné záznamy) and reload. A scraper that forgets this gets a well-formed page listing one ensemble where there are thirteen — a silent error, not a loud one. So: * one session is kept for the whole run and both switches are set first; * a **canary** is then fetched live: geo id 936, Uhlířské Janovice, must list ``Beseda (od 1873 do 1908)``, or the run stops (:class:`HistoryViewError`); * **every** page is checked before it is cached — each carries the switch buttons with the active one marked, so a session that expired mid-run is caught on the page where it happened (:func:`view_state`), re-established once, and otherwise fatal. Nothing is written to the cache unless it was served in the historical, full view. Per place, two pages are available: main.php?data=geo&id={geo_id} the place entry: type, okres, 'První zpráva', a chronicle, bibliography, archive citations — and, under 'Související Soubory', the ensembles with their years index.php?data=soubor&list=soubor11&id={geo_id} the ensemble list alone The place page's block is a superset: it prints each ensemble as ``Place: Name (span)`` and also lists the ensembles filed under *other* places — a town's parts, a touring group's other homes. Only the rows filed under the page's own heading are this place's (:func:`parse_place_ensembles`). Read that way the two pages agree — on all 91 places of the 2026-10-12 pilot for which both were fetched (:func:`compare_sources` re-checks it on whatever is cached) — so the default is ``pages=("geo",)``, one request per place, and ``pages=("geo", "list")`` is there for a cross-check. Step C — the ensemble pages --------------------------- ``index.php?data=soubor&id={ensemble_id}`` is the ensemble's own entry, and it says what the place page does not: ``Působení``, the **decades in which the ensemble is recorded active** (``188x, 189x, 190x``), its own founding and last-report fields, its own chronicle — the plays, venues and officers of *this* ensemble, not of the place — with bibliography and archive citations, and the people tied to it. It is served under the same session switches as the place pages and checked the same way before it is cached. At ~1.5 s a request the 34,154 ensembles are a day's run, so step C is meant for a selection: by default the ensembles that :func:`select_ensemble_ids` cannot rule out as starting before 1914 (certainly before, or a ``191x``/``19xx`` start that straddles it). What the dates are — and are not -------------------------------- ``První zpráva`` is the **first surviving report** of theatre in the place, not a founding date. An ensemble's span is printed as ``(od 1873 do 1908)``; the years may be fuzzy (``191x``, ``19xx``) or the span open-ended (``(od 1936)``). A fuzzy year is kept as its decade or century **with a precision flag** and its printed form beside it — it is never coerced to a year (:func:`parse_year_token`). Politeness ---------- The site is a small public-sector database behind Cloudflare; the client is built so that it cannot hurt it. * **Sequential, one connection**, never parallel. * **At least one second between requests** — ``delay`` below :data:`MIN_DELAY` is refused, the default is 1.5 s — and the pause **stretches with the server's own response time** (twice the last response time, capped), so a slow server is given room. * **Every response is cached on disk** and never requested twice; a re-run costs only the canary. * **Backs off** on 429/5xx (honouring ``Retry-After``), **gives up** after a run of consecutive failures (:class:`ServerUnhealthyError`) rather than hammering a server that is down, and **stops at once** on a Cloudflare challenge (:class:`BlockedError`) — bot protection is never worked around. * Rests ``batch_pause`` seconds every ``batch_size`` requests. * The ``User-Agent`` names this script and its version — a script, not a browser — and nothing about who runs it. * The site publishes no ``robots.txt`` (404 on 2026-10-12) and its pages carry ````. The parser extracts all label–value pairs generically, so new fields added by VÚA are captured automatically without code changes. Notes on the data source vuapraha.cz is the canonical VÚA -VHA Praha interface. The legionář database (~133k records) was assembled 1997–2004; the Habsburg fallen database has 186,194 records assembled 2012–2020. ID spaces are independent sequential integers with gaps; the ceiling must be probed empirically (see autodetect_max_id ). The site does not require authentication and individual record pages are server-rendered (no JS execution needed). The public search UI at /databaze-vha/?dtb=fallen-first is only a front door: it POSTs JSON to /wp-json/mo/v1/archive-database/html with a body of {page, name, surname, place, date, database} ( database="fallen-first" ) and returns {"html": <10-row results table>} whose rows link to the /padli-1-svetova/{id} detail pages enumerated here. Direct ID enumeration of the detail pages is simpler and yields the complete field set, so that endpoint is documented only as an optional manifest / cross-check source. TLS note: the server presents a Czech government-PKI certificate chain that modern OpenSSL rejects ("Basic Constraints of CA cert not marked critical"). Sessions therefore disable certificate verification by default; pass verify_tls=True (CLI --verify-tls ) to re-enable it. Detail-page field set (fallen DB): Příjmení, Jméno, Hodnost (often absent), Datum narození, Místo narození, Domovem, Příslušnost k útvaru rakousko-uherské armády, Datum úmrtí, Příčina úmrtí, Místo úmrtí, Bojiště, Místo pohřbení, Poznámka. The field set varies per record, so the CSV writer expands its header on the fly. "?" is the source's own null marker, stored verbatim. Scrapes individual record pages from two databases hosted at vuapraha.cz: legionari Databáze legionářů /legionari/{id}/ padli Databáze padlých v 1. sv. válce /padli-1-svetova/{id}/ Both databases share the same HTML structure: a sequence of ``div.inventory__item`` elements, each containing a label and a value. The parser extracts all label–value pairs generically, so new fields added by VÚA are captured automatically without code changes. Notes on the data source ------------------------ vuapraha.cz is the canonical VÚA-VHA Praha interface. The legionář database (~133k records) was assembled 1997–2004; the Habsburg fallen database has 186,194 records assembled 2012–2020. ID spaces are independent sequential integers with gaps; the ceiling must be probed empirically (see ``autodetect_max_id``). The site does not require authentication and individual record pages are server-rendered (no JS execution needed). The public search UI at ``/databaze-vha/?dtb=fallen-first`` is only a front door: it POSTs JSON to ``/wp-json/mo/v1/archive-database/html`` with a body of ``{page, name, surname, place, date, database}`` (``database="fallen-first"``) and returns ``{"html": <10-row results table>}`` whose rows link to the ``/padli-1-svetova/{id}`` detail pages enumerated here. Direct ID enumeration of the detail pages is simpler and yields the complete field set, so that endpoint is documented only as an optional manifest / cross-check source. TLS note: the server presents a Czech government-PKI certificate chain that modern OpenSSL rejects ("Basic Constraints of CA cert not marked critical"). Sessions therefore disable certificate verification by default; pass ``verify_tls=True`` (CLI ``--verify-tls``) to re-enable it. Detail-page field set (fallen DB): Příjmení, Jméno, Hodnost (often absent), Datum narození, Místo narození, Domovem, Příslušnost k útvaru rakousko-uherské armády, Datum úmrtí, Příčina úmrtí, Místo úmrtí, Bojiště, Místo pohřbení, Poznámka. script-utils-parsing-affiliations: TL;DR Parses the free-text Politická příslušnost field into per-party boolean dummies. v1.x built the party genealogy from Wikipedia; v2.0.0 rebuilds it on the Akademický atlas českých dějin , plate IV.37 ( Systém politických stran v českých zemích , p. 318) — a register of 55 parties of the Czech lands 1861–1918, each with its founding year, area of operation and a notes column recording every merger, renaming and dissolution. Transcribed and checked in reference/parties/ ( atlas_iv37_parties.csv , 12/12 invariants). Person parsing · v2.2.0 · 514 lines · 5 public functions · 5 constants · used by 02_data_cleaning.ipynb , 03_visualisation.ipynb , utils/parsing/schema.py +1 · utils/parsing/affiliations.py parse_affiliation atlas_codes affiliation_selftest add_affiliation_columns affiliation_report TOKEN_MAP REFUSED PARTY_ORDER PARTY_IDEOLOGY COL_PREFIX How it works Every token below carries the atlas code(s) that justify it, so a reader can go from a string in the data to a row in the printed register. What the atlas changed The "progressive" family is not a family. v1.x kept pokr as a separate Liberal bin. The register says three of the four pokrokové parties co-founded Č23 Česká státoprávní demokracie — Č13 (1918 spoluzakladatelka Č 23), Č15 (idem), Č17 (idem) — and Č23 was "1919 přejmenována na Národní demokracii". The fourth, Č7 radikálně pokroková , merged in 1908 into Č15, which also went to Č23. Masaryk's realists are the same line: Č12 Česká strana lidová ("realisté") "1905 transformace v Č 13". So a progressive token is evidence for nar_dem , not for a liberal party standing apart from it. pokr is gone as a canonical. lid.pokr. → nar_dem is confirmed , not merely inherited: Č17 Lidová strana pokroková (1909, Moravia) is a co-founder of Č23. real. → nar_dem is confirmed by the Č12 → Č13 → Č23 chain. Free Thought is not a party. volnomyšlenkář / volná myšlenka was folded into pokr ; it is a freethinker association and appears nowhere in the register. It is its own civic-org dummy now. What the atlas refuses to settle (see REFUSED ) A bare "lidová". Eight parties in the register carry it — Č3 (Moravian liberal-national), Č11 (Catholic), Č12 (Masaryk's realists), Č17, Č20, Č21, Č25, plus N4 and P6 — spanning Catholic, liberal-national and Masarykite. v1.x had no bare lid token; that silence was right, and it is now a documented refusal rather than a gap. Only the unambiguous Catholic spellings ( křesť.soc. , kat.nár. ) set lid . A bare "demokrat" / "dem." (39 records). Social democrat, national democrat and státoprávní demokracie all reduce to it. "SL" (108 records, the largest unmatched token) and every Slovak party. Plate IV.37 is v českých zemích — it contains no Slovak party at all, so it can neither confirm nor deny Slovenská liga or Hlinka's Slovenská ľudová strana . Needs a Slovak source; until then, unresolved. The three gymnastic organisations stay as dummies of their own sokol , orel and dtj are mobilisation proxies, not parties , and are never folded into an aligned party. Sokol is the mass Czech nationalist movement, Orel its Catholic counterpart, DTJ ( Dělnická tělovýchovná jednota ) the social-democratic one. Membership is a pre-war, revealed measure of which current a man had already joined — which is why it is worth a regressor of its own in a study of loyalty, and why it must not be read as a party statement. v1.x additionally asserted party alignments for them — Sokol → nar_dem , DTJ → soc_dem , Orel → lid — on the same Wikipedia reading as the party genealogy. Those claims are dropped, and the field itself is why. Of the 1,323 Sokol members who also name a party: 59 % national socialist (784), 18 % national democrat (236), 13 % social democrat (167), 9 % agrarian (115). The alignment was three times off. But the spread is not a defect in the proxy — it is what makes it one: Sokol ran across the Czech national parties rather than inside any of them, so the dummy measures nationalist mobilisation precisely because it does not resolve to a party. ⚠ Read the scale before using it. pol_sokol is 10,367 records — 26.1 % of every non-empty affiliation cell , the largest single value in the field — and on 87 % of them it is the only thing recorded. For most of those men the cell says "gymnast", not "voter". Any specification that treats pol_* as party affiliation must exclude the civic organisations; PARTY_IDEOLOGY marks them Civic org but nothing structurally stops a regression from mixing them in. DTJ is the same shape at a twentieth of the size (314 records, 77 % org-only); Orel is 8 records and carries nothing. Also dropped: rolník → agr . That mapped an occupation into a party dummy on the theory that a farmer self-describing is an Agrarian, while dělník in the same field mapped to nothing — an asymmetry with no source behind it, and the same error shape as D-43. """ affiliations.py — political affiliation, on the atlas's own genealogy ===================================================================== Parses the free-text ``Politická příslušnost`` field into per-party boolean dummies. v1.x built the party genealogy from Wikipedia; v2.0.0 rebuilds it on the **Akademický atlas českých dějin**, plate **IV.37** (*Systém politických stran v českých zemích*, p. 318) — a register of 55 parties of the Czech lands 1861–1918, each with its founding year, area of operation and a notes column recording every merger, renaming and dissolution. Transcribed and checked in ``reference/parties/`` (``atlas_iv37_parties.csv``, 12/12 invariants). Every token below carries the atlas code(s) that justify it, so a reader can go from a string in the data to a row in the printed register. What the atlas changed ---------------------- 1. **The "progressive" family is not a family.** v1.x kept ``pokr`` as a separate *Liberal* bin. The register says three of the four *pokrokové* parties co-founded Č23 *Česká státoprávní demokracie* — Č13 (1918 spoluzakladatelka Č 23), Č15 (idem), Č17 (idem) — and Č23 was "1919 přejmenována na Národní demokracii". The fourth, Č7 *radikálně pokroková*, merged in 1908 into Č15, which also went to Č23. Masaryk's realists are the same line: Č12 *Česká strana lidová* ("realisté") "1905 transformace v Č 13". So a progressive token is evidence for **nar_dem**, not for a liberal party standing apart from it. ``pokr`` is gone as a canonical. 2. ``lid.pokr.`` **→ nar_dem is confirmed**, not merely inherited: Č17 *Lidová strana pokroková* (1909, Moravia) is a co-founder of Č23. 3. ``real.`` **→ nar_dem is confirmed** by the Č12 → Č13 → Č23 chain. 4. **Free Thought is not a party.** ``volnomyšlenkář`` / ``volná myšlenka`` was folded into ``pokr``; it is a freethinker association and appears nowhere in the register. It is its own civic-org dummy now. What the atlas refuses to settle (see :data:`REFUSED`) ------------------------------------------------------ * **A bare "lidová".** Eight parties in the register carry it — Č3 (Moravian liberal-national), Č11 (Catholic), Č12 (Masaryk's realists), Č17, Č20, Č21, Č25, plus N4 and P6 — spanning Catholic, liberal-national and Masarykite. v1.x had no bare ``lid`` token; that silence was right, and it is now a documented refusal rather than a gap. Only the unambiguous Catholic spellings (``křesť.soc.``, ``kat.nár.``) set ``lid``. * **A bare "demokrat" / "dem."** (39 records). Social democrat, national democrat and *státoprávní demokracie* all reduce to it. * **"SL"** (108 records, the largest unmatched token) **and every Slovak party.** Plate IV.37 is *v českých zemích* — it contains no Slovak party at all, so it can neither confirm nor deny *Slovenská liga* or Hlinka's *Slovenská ľudová strana*. Needs a Slovak source; until then, unresolved. The three gymnastic organisations stay as dummies of their own ------------------------------------------------------------ ``sokol``, ``orel`` and ``dtj`` are **mobilisation proxies, not parties**, and are never folded into an aligned party. Sokol is the mass **Czech nationalist** movement, Orel its Catholic counterpart, DTJ (*Dělnická tělovýchovná jednota*) the social-democratic one. Membership is a pre-war, revealed measure of which current a man had already joined — which is why it is worth a regressor of its own in a study of loyalty, and why it must not be read as a party statement. v1.x additionally asserted party *alignments* for them — Sokol → ``nar_dem``, DTJ → ``soc_dem``, Orel → ``lid`` — on the same Wikipedia reading as the party genealogy. Those claims are dropped, and the field itself is why. Of the **1,323** Sokol members who also name a party: **59 %** national socialist (784), 18 % national democrat (236), 13 % social democrat (167), 9 % agrarian (115). The alignment was three times off. But the *spread* is not a defect in the proxy — it is what makes it one: Sokol ran **across** the Czech national parties rather than inside any of them, so the dummy measures nationalist mobilisation precisely because it does not resolve to a party. ⚠ **Read the scale before using it.** ``pol_sokol`` is 10,367 records — **26.1 % of every non-empty affiliation cell**, the largest single value in the field — and on **87 %** of them it is the *only* thing recorded. For most of those men the cell says "gymnast", not "voter". Any specification that treats ``pol_*`` as party affiliation must exclude the civic organisations; :data:`PARTY_IDEOLOGY` marks them ``Civic org`` but nothing structurally stops a regression from mixing them in. DTJ is the same shape at a twentieth of the size (314 records, 77 % org-only); Orel is 8 records and carries nothing. Also dropped: ``rolník`` → ``agr``. That mapped an **occupation** into a party dummy on the theory that a farmer self-describing is an Agrarian, while ``dělník`` in the same field mapped to nothing — an asymmetry with no source behind it, and the same error shape as D-43. TL;DR Vzdělání is not a level . It is an itinerary : a sequence of school types, each optionally followed by the number of years completed ( ob. 5 mě. 3 pok. 3 = five years Volksschule, three Bürgerschule, three years of the apprentices' continuation school). v1.0.0 collapsed the string with first-match substring rules and got the ladder wrong in three places; this module tokenises the itinerary instead and reports the highest rung reached, the years spent at each, and the track. Person parsing · v2.1.0 · 620 lines · 6 public functions · 5 constants · used by 02_data_cleaning.ipynb , 03_visualisation.ipynb , utils/parsing/schema.py +4 · utils/parsing/education.py parse_education clean_education add_education_column education_selftest ladder_report education_report EDUC_ORDER EDUC_ORDINAL TRACKS INSTITUTIONS TIE_BREAK How it works The ladder below is the settlement of the Reichsvolksschulgesetz of 14 May 1869, still standing in 1914 — the law under which every man in the sample was schooled (birth cohorts ≈ 1875–1900). Sources and page citations live in reference/EDUCATION_LADDER.md : Moore (2020) Teaching the Empire — the general ladder. Compulsory schooling is ages 6–14, reached as ob. 5 + mě. 3 ; Gymnasium (8 yrs) and Realschule (7 yrs) are entered at age ten, in parallel with the Bürgerschule, not after it; the Lehrerbildungsanstalt is entered from the Bürgerschule at fifteen and is deliberately not an academic track. Lassnigg (2015) IHS WP 108 — the vocational branch. The pokračovací (gewerbliche Fortbildungsschule ) was legally part of compulsory mass schooling , governed communally alongside the Volksschule, and it selected on nothing : apprenticeship required no educational credential, and the school obligation followed the contract. The full-time vocational schools ( obch. , prům. , odb. , hosp. ) required Bürgerschule grades plus an entrance exam, so they do sit above it. Three consequences, and they are the whole point of the rewrite: pok. does not raise the ordinal. It is recorded as a track flag ( educ_apprentice , 8,815 records) and a year count. Under v1.0.0 it scored Upper secondary , putting 8,117 records — the classic apprentice itinerary — in the same bucket as gym. uč.ústav sits one rung below the Matura tracks, not level with them. The ordinal is highest institution attended , not "level achieved". Completion is a separate, explicitly missing-able column, because a bare reálka does not say whether the man finished. Two limits, both inherited from the sources and both documented in EDUCATION_LADDER.md §5: Duration is unknown for the vocational rungs. Fortbildungsschule hours and Fachschule course lengths varied by Land and trade (regional laws 1907–1931), so educ_complete is pd.NA for them rather than guessed, and no educ_years_total is emitted. Do not sum the year columns. Cisleithania only. Both sources are silent on Hungary, whose schools the Ausgleich handed to Budapest (Eötvös 1868, Apponyi 1907). Slovak and Rusyn births are parsed on the same tokens because the strings are Czech, but the ordinal is not established for them — interact it with a Cisleithanian/Transleithanian indicator, the way birth_okres and birth_jaras are kept apart. What 2.1.0 changed Every institution must start at a word start. The scan was an unanchored substring test, so technik matched inside hydrotechnika and ob inside pob. — the shape ranks 1.4.0 had to remove after Fidler caught generálmajor scoring as major . The number group stays unanchored so "reálka4" still yields 4. Ties on the top rung are broken by a written rule , TIE_BREAK (D-51). 1,512 records name two schools on one rung, and max alone resolved them by which one the clerk wrote first — the same pair landing both ways. Semesters are not years. sem. / semestr and its number are lifted out into educ_semesters (722 records) before the itinerary is scanned; they used to be written into educ_years_secondary as if they were years. střední yields to a named school. It states the level , not the school, so "stř. hosp. škola" is an agricultural Fachschule (83 records). The imputed rung is flagged. Where only a continuation school is named the ordinal is floored at Elementary; those 1,112 records now carry educ_top_imputed and the track continuation , because educ_top there names a school educ_institutions does not list. level**. It is an *itinerary*: a sequence of school types, each optionally followed by the number of years completed (``ob. 5 mě. 3 pok. 3`` = five years Volksschule, three Bürgerschule, three years of the apprentices' continuation school). v1.0.0 collapsed the string with first-match substring rules and got the ladder wrong in three places; this module tokenises the itinerary instead and reports the highest rung reached, the years spent at each, and the track. The ladder below is the settlement of the **Reichsvolksschulgesetz** of 14 May 1869, still standing in 1914 — the law under which every man in the sample was schooled (birth cohorts ≈ 1875–1900). Sources and page citations live in ``reference/EDUCATION_LADDER.md``: * Moore (2020) *Teaching the Empire* — the general ladder. Compulsory schooling is ages 6–14, reached as ``ob. 5`` + ``mě. 3``; Gymnasium (8 yrs) and Realschule (7 yrs) are entered at **age ten, in parallel with** the Bürgerschule, not after it; the Lehrerbildungsanstalt is entered *from* the Bürgerschule at fifteen and is deliberately not an academic track. * Lassnigg (2015) IHS WP 108 — the vocational branch. The *pokračovací* (gewerbliche **Fortbildungsschule**) was legally **part of compulsory mass schooling**, governed communally alongside the Volksschule, and it selected on *nothing*: apprenticeship required no educational credential, and the school obligation followed the contract. The full-time vocational schools (``obch.``, ``prům.``, ``odb.``, ``hosp.``) required Bürgerschule grades plus an entrance exam, so they do sit above it. Three consequences, and they are the whole point of the rewrite: 1. ``pok.`` **does not raise the ordinal.** It is recorded as a track flag (``educ_apprentice``, 8,815 records) and a year count. Under v1.0.0 it scored *Upper secondary*, putting 8,117 records — the classic apprentice itinerary — in the same bucket as ``gym.`` 2. ``uč.ústav`` sits one rung below the Matura tracks, not level with them. 3. The ordinal is **highest institution attended**, not "level achieved". Completion is a separate, explicitly missing-able column, because a bare ``reálka`` does not say whether the man finished. Two limits, both inherited from the sources and both documented in ``EDUCATION_LADDER.md`` §5: * **Duration is unknown for the vocational rungs.** Fortbildungsschule hours and Fachschule course lengths varied by Land and trade (regional laws 1907–1931), so ``educ_complete`` is ``pd.NA`` for them rather than guessed, and no ``educ_years_total`` is emitted. Do not sum the year columns. * **Cisleithania only.** Both sources are silent on Hungary, whose schools the Ausgleich handed to Budapest (Eötvös 1868, Apponyi 1907). Slovak and Rusyn births are parsed on the same tokens because the *strings* are Czech, but the ordinal is not established for them — interact it with a Cisleithanian/Transleithanian indicator, the way ``birth_okres`` and ``birth_jaras`` are kept apart. TL;DR Collapses the free-text rank fields onto within-system ordinal scales — the k.u.k. Dienstgrade hierarchy ( system="habsburg" , 1–20) and the Czechoslovak Legion / early-ČSA ladder ( system="legion" , 1–14). The Habsburg ladder is taken from reference/ranks/rank_ladders.md §A, validated against the bilingual Czech↔German table in Pod císařským praporem p.408: 1 vojín (+ branch privates) Infanterist / Kanonier / … 2 svobodník, nápředník, závodčí Gefreiter / Oberkanonier / Patrouilleführer 3 desátník Korporal 4 četař Zugsführer 5 šikovatel, strážmistr Feldwebel / Wachtmeister 6 kadet Kadett ┐ officer-candidate band 7 praporčík Fähnrich │ (6–9 reconstructed — 8 důstojnický zástupce Offizierstellvertr│ p.408 treats it as a 9 kadet-aspirant Kadettaspirant ┘ band, hedge via tier) 10 poručík Leutnant 11 nadporučík Oberleutnant 12 setník (hejtman/rytmistr/kapitán) Hauptmann 13 major / 14 podplukovník / 15 plukovník 16 generálmajor … 20 polní maršál Design notes The j.d. token ( jednoroční dobrovolník / Einjährig-Freiwilliger) is a status, not a rank (§E): it is stripped before matching and returned as a boolean flag. Progression entries ("podporučík, poručík", "vojín, desátník") keep both ends: *_ord = highest reached, *_ord_low = lowest listed. podporučík is not a k.u.k. rank (§A note); under system="habsburg" it is dropped to <NA> and surfaced in the residual report (do not score it as an officer). Under system="legion" it is a real rank (sub-Leutnant, ord 8). rotmistr is likewise not a k.u.k. rank (the cavalry captain is rytmistr = Rittmeister): Habsburg rotmistr → <NA> ; Legion rotmistr is a senior NCO / warrant grade (ord 6, §B). Every lookup is keyed by system (rules, ordinals, drop-tokens, and tiers all differ): the §F harmonization trap ( poručík = Leutnant here but a different OF slot in the Legion) is exactly why the two ladders never share a table. Legion generals exist (ord 15–17, §B-gen) — unlike the Habsburg generals, which are in the ladder for completeness at n = 0. Both naming systems occur: Russian ( generálmajor , generálporučík ) and post-1918 ČSA French ( brigádní/divizní/ armádní generál ), paired by NATO grade. Bare "generál" is refused (tier, not grade). Rule tokens must match at a word start ( _at_word_start ). Substring matching alone let a longer word silently resolve to a shorter rank it embedded — generálmajor → major, generálporučík → poručík, aspirant na podporučíka → poručík. Genuine compounds ( nadstrážmistr , novobranec , nadělostřelec , …) are listed as their own tokens; anything else now surfaces as unresolved instead of being assigned a plausible wrong grade. the free-text rank fields onto **within-system ordinal** scales — the k.u.k. *Dienstgrade* hierarchy (``system="habsburg"``, 1–20) and the Czechoslovak Legion / early-ČSA ladder (``system="legion"``, 1–14). The motivating use is the thesis's *relative rank deprivation* measure, so the ordinal is the headline output. ⚠️ The two ordinal (``*_ord``) scales are **within-system** and are *not* directly subtractable (``rank_ladders.md`` intro, §F): a Habsburg *poručík* (ord 10) and a Legion *poručík* (ord 9) are the **same** OF‑1 grade. The cross-system reset instead bridges via the shared name-anchored **common** scale (ALT 1, §G): ``add_rank_columns`` also emits ``{prefix}_common`` (system-blind grade) and ``{prefix}_band`` (coarse NATO OF/OR band), and :func:`add_rank_reset` differences the *common* columns to build ``rank_reset = legion_common − habsburg_common`` (never the within-system ordinals). The Habsburg ladder is taken from ``reference/ranks/rank_ladders.md`` §A, validated against the bilingual Czech↔German table in *Pod císařským praporem* p.408: 1 vojín (+ branch privates) Infanterist / Kanonier / … 2 svobodník, nápředník, závodčí Gefreiter / Oberkanonier / Patrouilleführer 3 desátník Korporal 4 četař Zugsführer 5 šikovatel, strážmistr Feldwebel / Wachtmeister 6 kadet Kadett ┐ officer-candidate band 7 praporčík Fähnrich │ (6–9 reconstructed — 8 důstojnický zástupce Offizierstellvertr│ p.408 treats it as a 9 kadet-aspirant Kadettaspirant ┘ band, hedge via tier) 10 poručík Leutnant 11 nadporučík Oberleutnant 12 setník (hejtman/rytmistr/kapitán) Hauptmann 13 major / 14 podplukovník / 15 plukovník 16 generálmajor … 20 polní maršál Design notes ------------ * The ``j.d.`` token (*jednoroční dobrovolník* / Einjährig-Freiwilliger) is a **status, not a rank** (§E): it is stripped before matching and returned as a boolean flag. * Progression entries ("podporučík, poručík", "vojín, desátník") keep **both** ends: ``*_ord`` = highest reached, ``*_ord_low`` = lowest listed. * ``podporučík`` is **not** a k.u.k. rank (§A note); under ``system="habsburg"`` it is dropped to ``<NA>`` and surfaced in the residual report (do not score it as an officer). Under ``system="legion"`` it **is** a real rank (sub-Leutnant, ord 8). * ``rotmistr`` is likewise **not** a k.u.k. rank (the cavalry captain is *rytmistr* = Rittmeister): Habsburg ``rotmistr`` → ``<NA>``; Legion ``rotmistr`` is a senior NCO / warrant grade (ord 6, §B). * Every lookup is keyed by ``system`` (rules, ordinals, drop-tokens, and tiers all differ): the §F harmonization trap (*poručík* = Leutnant here but a different OF slot in the Legion) is exactly why the two ladders never share a table. * **Legion generals exist** (ord 15–17, §B-gen) — unlike the Habsburg generals, which are in the ladder for completeness at n = 0. Both naming systems occur: Russian (*generálmajor*, *generálporučík*) and post-1918 ČSA French (*brigádní/divizní/ armádní generál*), paired by NATO grade. Bare "generál" is refused (tier, not grade). * Rule tokens must match at a **word start** (:func:`_at_word_start`). Substring matching alone let a longer word silently resolve to a shorter rank it embedded — *generálmajor* → major, *generálporučík* → poručík, *aspirant na podporučíka* → poručík. Genuine compounds (*nadstrážmistr*, *novobranec*, *nadělostřelec*, …) are listed as their own tokens; anything else now surfaces as unresolved instead of being assigned a plausible wrong grade. The cleaning notebook ( 02_data_cleaning , §1 legion and §2 habsburg) and the eventual master notebook call to_english as the last step of their cleaning pipeline to turn a mixed Czech-raw / English-parsed DataFrame into a pruned, fully-English, analysis-ready table written to data/final/ . Person parsing · v1.13.0 · 651 lines · 3 public functions · 4 constants · used by 02_data_cleaning.ipynb , 15_frozen_run.ipynb , utils/validation/data_checks.py · utils/parsing/schema.py to_english schema_report write_data_dictionary LEGION_RENAME LEGION_FINAL HABSBURG_RENAME HABSBURG_FINAL How it works Two datasets are supported via the dataset argument: "legion" — legionnaire records ( csol.cz ), 02_data_cleaning §1. "habsburg" — fallen Habsburg soldiers ( VÚA ), 02_data_cleaning §2. Design *_RENAME maps the current column name (raw Czech or a parser's English output) to its final snake_case name. Only columns we keep need an entry; everything unmapped is dropped by the FINAL selection. *_FINAL is the ordered list of final columns to keep. Boolean dummy families with a fixed, known code set ( exit_* , cause_* ) are enumerated explicitly; the data-driven political-affiliation dummies ( pol_* ) are appended dynamically by to_english . The legionnaire theater ( utils.parsing.theater ) and the Habsburg theatre ( utils.parsing.habsburg ) are unified to the column name theater . The label sets differ — the Legion's service theatres (Russia / Italy / France / Serbia/Balkans / Britain/Dominions / Post-war (ČSA)) against the fronts a Habsburg soldier died on (Russia / Italy / Serbia / Macedonia / Romania / France / Rear) — so only Russia, Italy and France compare directly. What "before 1914" means when a year is fuzzy An ensemble's start is printed as a year, a decade ( 191x ) or a century ( 19xx ) and is carried with its precision. starts_before is the single rule: year 1913 -> yes 1914 -> no decade 190x (≤1909) -> yes 191x (1910–19) -> ambiguous 192x -> no century 18xx (≤1899) -> yes 19xx -> ambiguous "Before 1914" in every table below means yes — the ambiguous are counted and shown beside it, never folded in. The join A database place (present-day obec / místní část, with coordinates) is tied to a row of settlements_1910 (the ČSÚ lexikon crosswalk; coordinates for about half the obce and few hamlets) in three tiers, most trusted first: name+coords same normalised name, both geocoded, ≤ `max_km` apart name+okres same normalised name, the settlement not geocoded, and the place's present-day okres on the settlement's okres timeline (`okres_all`) — accepted only where that leaves exactly one candidate on each side fuzzy+coords names ≥ `min_similarity` alike, ≤ `fuzzy_km` apart The match is one-to-one on both sides and the result has exactly one row per place — both asserted. settlements_1910 has no declared key (a name can be an obec and an osada in the same okres), so its row position is used as settlement_row . Town size There is no settlement-level 1910 population in the repo (the ČSÚ lexikon volume that carries it is a PDF whose digits do not extract), so size is proxied by three classes read off what the crosswalk does carry: the seat of a 1910 judicial district, any other commune, and a dependent hamlet or part. If the settlements frame is given a population_1910 column, coverage_tables bands on that instead. The chronicle (0.2.0) Each place's chronicle_text is a run of notes, one per line, two in three opening with a date ( 1895-1938 DS Sokola , Od 1881 , Koncem 19. stol. , V 80. letech ). chronicle_lines reads every line into a table keyed (geo_id, line_no) : its kind (dated event , undated note, periodical citation , the database's admin note on the present okres, heading , separator ), its leading date as start and end intervals (so 191x , kolem 1850 and před 1900 each keep their width), the associations it names and whether it is puppet theatre. Rules only; a bare decade takes its century from the dated line above it, and century_inference_check measures that rule where the century is printed. Nothing here is written to data/final . Clauses (0.4.0) One line is often several events ( 1887-1934 SDO, 1914 32 členů. ), so chronicle_clauses cuts each note wherever a new date opens after a comma, a semicolon or a full stop — never inside brackets, a quoted title, the line's leading date, or a dated newspaper report — keyed (geo_id, line_no, clause_no) . Each clause carries its own date interval, the other years it prints, and the EVENT_CUES its words point to: the codebook's draft, which the author rules on before any of it is a code (D-140). The measure (0.5.0) The author ruled each type's role and twelve design calls (D-141; CODEBOOK_ROLES and the constants beside it). code_clauses applies them; evidence_table puts the ensemble list, the coded clauses and the first reports into one interval form and gives each company one company_id across sources; place_year_panel turns that into Czech amateur theatre per place and year, 1780–1913, every measure certain and possible ; area_year_tables sums it to the 1910 settlement, court and okres. Written to data/interim/theatre/ by the pilot runner; nothing reaches the persons. Ensemble pages (0.6.0) An ensemble's own page (scraper step C) gives the decades it was active ( Působení ), an end or last report, and a chronicle of its own. By the author's rulings (D-145): a listed decade makes the company possible across it, never certain, and a page that lists decades replaces B1's open end, so the company is possible only in those decades (a "…" gap adds nothing); a printed end closes the span, certain from start to end; and the ensemble's chronicle is cut and coded like a place's, its company clauses tied to that ensemble ( ensemble_chronicle_clauses ). A company's possible years are the union of its records' ranges, no longer the hull, so a gap between two decades stays empty. ==================================================================================== **Feasibility pilot.** Nothing here feeds ``data/final``. The module takes the two tables written by :mod:`utils.scraping.scraper_amaterskedivadlo` (places, ensembles) and asks the one question that decides whether the source is worth building on: *how evenly is it documented* — across town sizes, across Bohemia and Moravia, across Czech- and German-speaking districts — before any of it is read as a measure of associational life. (Not to be confused with :mod:`utils.parsing.theater`, which is the *war* theatre — Russia / Italy / France.) What "before 1914" means when a year is fuzzy --------------------------------------------- An ensemble's start is printed as a year, a decade (``191x``) or a century (``19xx``) and is carried with its precision. :func:`starts_before` is the single rule: year 1913 -> yes 1914 -> no decade 190x (≤1909) -> yes 191x (1910–19) -> ambiguous 192x -> no century 18xx (≤1899) -> yes 19xx -> ambiguous "Before 1914" in every table below means **yes** — the ambiguous are counted and shown beside it, never folded in. The join -------- A database place (present-day obec / místní část, with coordinates) is tied to a row of ``settlements_1910`` (the ČSÚ lexikon crosswalk; coordinates for about half the obce and few hamlets) in three tiers, most trusted first: name+coords same normalised name, both geocoded, ≤ ``max_km`` apart name+okres same normalised name, the settlement not geocoded, and the place's present-day okres on the settlement's okres timeline (``okres_all``) — accepted only where that leaves exactly one candidate on each side fuzzy+coords names ≥ ``min_similarity`` alike, ≤ ``fuzzy_km`` apart The match is one-to-one on both sides and the result has exactly one row per place — both asserted. ``settlements_1910`` has no declared key (a name can be an *obec* and an *osada* in the same okres), so its row position is used as ``settlement_row``. Town size --------- There is **no settlement-level 1910 population in the repo** (the ČSÚ lexikon volume that carries it is a PDF whose digits do not extract), so size is proxied by three classes read off what the crosswalk does carry: the seat of a 1910 judicial district, any other commune, and a dependent hamlet or part. If the settlements frame is given a ``population_1910`` column, :func:`coverage_tables` bands on that instead. The chronicle (0.2.0) --------------------- Each place's ``chronicle_text`` is a run of notes, one per line, two in three opening with a date (``1895-1938 DS Sokola``, ``Od 1881``, ``Koncem 19. stol.``, ``V 80. letech``). :func:`chronicle_lines` reads every line into a table keyed ``(geo_id, line_no)``: its kind (dated *event*, *undated* note, periodical *citation*, the database's *admin* note on the present okres, *heading*, *separator*), its leading date as start and end **intervals** (so ``191x``, ``kolem 1850`` and ``před 1900`` each keep their width), the associations it names and whether it is puppet theatre. Rules only; a bare decade takes its century from the dated line above it, and :func:`century_inference_check` measures that rule where the century is printed. Nothing here is written to ``data/final``. Clauses (0.4.0) --------------- One line is often several events (``1887-1934 SDO, 1914 32 členů.``), so :func:`chronicle_clauses` cuts each note wherever a new date opens after a comma, a semicolon or a full stop — never inside brackets, a quoted title, the line's leading date, or a dated newspaper report — keyed ``(geo_id, line_no, clause_no)``. Each clause carries its own date interval, the other years it prints, and the :data:`EVENT_CUES` its words point to: the codebook's draft, which the author rules on before any of it is a code (D-140). The measure (0.5.0) ------------------- The author ruled each type's role and twelve design calls (D-141; :data:`CODEBOOK_ROLES` and the constants beside it). :func:`code_clauses` applies them; :func:`evidence_table` puts the ensemble list, the coded clauses and the first reports into one interval form and gives each company one ``company_id`` across sources; :func:`place_year_panel` turns that into Czech amateur theatre per place and year, 1780–1913, every measure *certain* and *possible*; :func:`area_year_tables` sums it to the 1910 settlement, court and okres. Written to ``data/interim/theatre/`` by the pilot runner; nothing reaches the persons. Ensemble pages (0.6.0) ---------------------- An ensemble's own page (scraper step C) gives the decades it was active (*Působení*), an end or last report, and a chronicle of its own. By the author's rulings (D-145): a listed decade makes the company *possible* across it, never certain, and a page that lists decades replaces B1's open end, so the company is possible only in those decades (a "…" gap adds nothing); a printed end closes the span, certain from start to end; and the ensemble's chronicle is cut and coded like a place's, its company clauses tied to that ensemble (:func:`ensemble_chronicle_clauses`). A company's possible years are the union of its records' ranges, no longer the hull, so a gap between two decades stays empty. script-utils-parsing-census: TL;DR Harmonises the Rumpler-Seger / MPIDR census workbooks in data/raw/census/ and joins them to utils.parsing.districts ( districts_1910 ) by exact unit code — the census IDCourtdistr equals our court_id (339/339) and IDPoldistrict equals our okres_id ( region·1000 + district ). No name matching. Geography & census · v1.3.0 · 507 lines · 8 public functions · 3 constants · used by 02_data_cleaning.ipynb , 03_visualisation.ipynb , utils/parsing/census_labels.py +1 · utils/parsing/census.py load_census_file build_census_panel okres_census_crosswalk pool_twin_okresy blank_twin_members build_census_panels add_census_okres_id census_report CZECH_LAND_CODES STEM_PREFIX FILE_PREFIX How it works Each workbook has a data sheet (ID columns + value columns) and a Variable Names sheet giving the multi-row, merged-cell German header for each value column. Value columns are named by topic + index ( Religion1..18 , Umgspr1..11 , Gebor1.. , Beruf1.. …) — the one exception is the district-court justice caseload file, whose columns are generic V1..V91 . Naming ( _column_names ) The Variable Names sheet is read with openpyxl so merged cells are expanded exactly (a de-merged pandas read would let a deep label such as helvetischen Bekenntnisses bleed into the next column). ==================================================================================== The Cisleithanian census (:mod:`utils.parsing.census`) carries **German** variable names (``umgspr_bohmisch_mahrisch_slowakisch``) and the Transleithanian one (:mod:`utils.parsing.census_hu`) **Magyar** ones (``etn_tot_anyanyelv``). This module renames every covariate to an English ``snake_case`` label and adds analysis-ready shares/rates. Two-stage translation ---------------------- 1. **Curated** clean names for the analytically-central families — colloquial language (``lang_*``), religion (``rel_*``), literacy/disability (``lit_*`` / ``disab_*``), and the settlement-size population breakdown (``pop_*``). See ``CURATED_CIS`` / ``CURATED_HU``. 2. **Compositional** token translation for the long tail (births, deaths, cause of death, livestock, occupation, justice, savings) via ``DE_TOKENS`` / ``HU_TOKENS`` — the family prefix is kept, content tokens translated, grammatical stopwords dropped, and any residual name collisions are disambiguated with a numeric suffix so the mapping stays 1-to-1. Derived shares (fractions of the relevant base) are added by :func:`add_shares_cis` / :func:`add_shares_hu`: language shares, key religion shares, literacy rate, illegitimacy rate, infant-mortality proxy — the ratios that go on the RHS. TL;DR Builds the authoritative 1910 district crosswalk for the Czech crown lands from the MPIDR / Rumpler-Seger GIS boundary file ( reference/places/mpidr/ ) — the spine — with curated Czech names from reference/places/district_cs_curation.csv . Geography & census · v1.2.0 · 410 lines · 7 public functions · 3 constants · used by 02_data_cleaning.ipynb , utils/docs/build_docs.py , utils/parsing/districts_hu.py +2 · utils/parsing/districts.py read_dbf parse_mpidr attach_gazetteer_names build_district_backbone write_curation_template districts_report validate_against_code LAND_MAP OKRES_DE_OVERRIDE GERMAN_NAME_FIX How it works Why MPIDR is the spine The MPIDR shapefile ( MPIDR & CGG 2012, after Rumpler & Seger 2010 ) is a clean, complete polygon layer of the 1910 census administrative units with a stable 3-level hierarchy encoded in ID_1 = REGION·10^6 + DISTRICT·10^3 + LOCAL_ : LAND (crown land) → DISTRICT (political okres) → LOCAL_ (Gerichtsbezirk / soudní okres) so it authoritatively fixes which court districts belong to which political okres , carries stable geo-IDs + polygons (the census-merge key and the spatial backbone), and its German names are clean apart from six transliterations repaired by GERMAN_NAME_FIX ( Sziszkow = Žižkow). Czech names — provenance Each district's canonical Czech name ( *_cs ) is resolved, best-first: curated ( district_cs_curation.csv ) — the accented canonical form; all 330 court and 158 okres names are curated, so this is the only tier in use; MPIDR de-accented Czech (the NAME field's post-slash part) — a fallback that is the right name minus diacritics, flagged needs_review . The OCR Ortsverzeichnis gazetteer once supplied a third tier; its Czech district names proved unusable ("Bude jo vice") and it is archived ( _archive/gazetteer.py ). attach_gazetteer_names is kept only for that history. Note on the city/rural twins: both members of a pair carry the same okres_de (the seat court's German name, e.g. Olmuetz ); okres_cs is what tells them apart ( Olomouc / Olomouc (město) ). Geography & census · v1.6.0 · 372 lines · 3 public functions · used by 02_data_cleaning.ipynb · utils/parsing/lexikon.py parse_lexikon build_settlement_crosswalk lexikon_report How it works The register is a narrative: each entry is keyed by an ALL-CAPS modern Czech headword and lists the settlement's status + okres for every census year, e.g. :: BLATEC v r. 1869-1910 obec v okr. Olomouc, v r. 1921-1930 obec v okr. Olomouc-venkov, … ABERTAMY v r. 1869-1930 pod názvem Abertham město v okr. Nejdek, … For each entry we extract the segment whose year range contains 1910 (note 1900-1950 covers 1910 without the literal year) and read off: cs_name the headword — the modern Czech settlement name; name_1910 the pod názvem … form used in 1910 — the historical name , which for Sudeten settlements is the German exonym ( Abertham , Adolfsgrün , Olbersdorf ) and elsewhere an older Czech spelling; okres_1910 the 1910 political okres (period name), mapped to okres_id via utils.parsing.records_geo (exact okres/court names + fuzzy); status_1910 obec (independent commune) / osada (hamlet) / cast (part-of), with parent_1910 the parent commune where the settlement was dependent. Cross-reference stubs ( HEADWORD viz Target (Okres) ) are returned separately as an alias table (alternative/older spelling → canonical name) — useful for resolving record spellings. Because the register tracks the okres for every census year, the resulting settlement → okres_1910 map also recovers records whose birth_okres is a post-1910 administrative label (e.g. Praha-venkov , Kralupy nad Vltavou ): resolve the settlement, not the anachronistic okres. ===================================================================== Maps a soldier's birth district string (``birth_okres``) to the 1910 political-okres identifier (``okres_id`` = ``region·1000 + district``) of :mod:`utils.parsing.districts` (``districts_1910``), so the okres-level census panel (:mod:`utils.parsing.census`) can be joined on. Why this is not a plain equality join ------------------------------------- The csol.cz / VÚA ``birth_okres`` field mixes **two** administrative levels: * the **political okres** (politický okres) — e.g. ``Most``, ``Trutnov`` — which is the census unit, *and* * the **court district** (soudní okres / Gerichtsbezirk) — e.g. ``Hořovice`` (which sat in political okres *Beroun*), ``Falknov nad Ohří`` (in *Loket*), ``Nymburk`` (in *Poděbrady*). So the lookup is built from **both** the political-okres names (``okres_cs`` / ``okres_cs_modern`` / ``okres_de``) and the court names (``gerichtsbezirk_cs`` / ``…_modern`` / ``…_de``), every one resolving to its **parent** ``okres_id``. Political-okres names take priority where a name is shared with a court in a different okres (the city/rural pairs, e.g. *Olomouc* vs *Olomouc (město)*, whose seat court carries the same name in both units). City/rural twins ---------------- Ten seats name **two** units, a statutory city and the rural district around it. A district string alone cannot tell them apart, so :func:`add_birth_okres_id` resolves the bare name to the **rural** unit throughout, a trailing rural qualifier (``Olomouc venkov``) is stripped by rule rather than by fuzzy accident, and :func:`resolve_twin_pairs` then promotes to the city unit exactly those records whose *municipality* is the city itself. See DECISIONS D-17. Greater Prague — a 1922 boundary written onto 1910 records ---------------------------------------------------------- Prague absorbed 37 municipalities on 1 January 1922, and **both** person databases were compiled afterwards. A clerk copying the card of a man born in Žižkov in 1890 wrote the okres he knew — *Praha* — for a town that in 1910 was the seat of its own political okres. The ``okres`` tier matches that outright and never consults the municipality, so those records carried inner-Prague census covariates. :func:`resolve_prague_suburbs` sends them to the 1910 okres their municipality actually had, from the curated ``reference/places/prague_suburb_curation.csv``. Same shape as the twin rule — the municipality decides — but not the same thing: a twin pair coexisted in 1910, whereas here one unit swallowed the others twelve years later. Carried in ``{prefix}_okres_prague`` (``city`` / ``suburb``). See DECISIONS D-36. Match tiers (``birth_okres_match``) ----------------------------------- ``okres`` matched a political-okres name (strongest) ``court`` matched a court-district name → its parent okres ``fuzzy`` token-set ratio ≥ *threshold* to a lookup key (near-exact variants such as ``Teplice-Šanov`` → *Teplice*). A tie at the top score means the cell names more than one district; it is broken by the record's own **municipality**, else by the Prague-suburb rule, else refused (DECISIONS D-23) ``alias`` resolved via a curated :data:`ALIAS_OVERRIDE` entry ``<NA>`` no confident match — overwhelmingly a birthplace **outside** the Czech-lands 1910 census frame (Slovakia, Hungary, Vienna, Galicia, Russia) or an okres created after 1910; these individuals legitimately have no Cisleithanian census covariate. This is the finer juridical layer the name-based okres matcher ( utils.parsing.records_geo ) cannot resolve — a court is a sub -okres unit, so it can only be fixed geometrically. Validation: of the settlements carrying both a court and a name-based okres_id , the court's okres agrees with the name 90.0 % of the time on containment alone (build of 2026-09-23) and ~96 % after the D-35 near-miss repair — which agrees by construction on the rows it snaps, so the QA gate counts those rows as the disagreements they were (audit 2026-09-22 §B9). The 68 % first measured on 2026-07-16 was not structural, as this note once claimed: it was a coordinate bug — a third of geocodes came from an unguarded unique-name fallback (audit 2026-07-16 §D2). Treat court_id as a complementary juridical layer ; the analysis-grade okres key remains the name-based okres_id . .. warning:: Until 2026-08-05 this note also claimed that central-Prague coordinates "correctly land in the separate 1910 okresy Královské Vinohrady / Nusle / Vršovice, not okres Praha — verified". That was wrong, and it hid a defect for three weeks. Staré Město was inside the 1910 city; the reason the coordinate landed in Vinohrady is that the MPIDR polygon for Prague — the right size , 20.8 km² against ~21 km² — has its eastern edge drawn some 500 m too far west. The name test (v1.3.0) Surname and given name are scored separately , each on a phonetic key that folds the Czech/German orthography the two archives mix ( sch →s, tsch / cz / tz / z →c, w →v, ph →f, th →t, y / ie →i, doubled letters): the surname must reach a token_set_ratio of SURNAME_MIN ( SURNAME_MIN_CORROBORATED when the birth okres agrees too) and the given name GIVEN_MIN . Until v1.2.x one token_sort_ratio over the concatenated "surname given" string had to reach 80, and a long common given name carried the pair on its own: STANĚK František ↔ Soja František scored exactly 80. On the 2026-09-03 build, 263 DOB-confirmed and 126 note-confirmed pairs had surnames less than 60 % alike (BERAN↔Bureš, ČERNÝ↔Cvrk), and 111 VÚA records were claimed by two to four different legionnaires — one Zdice-born František by Šůra, Škvára, Schoř and Šinágl (audit 2026-09-22 §A1). Precision-first confirmed-overlap rule. A pair counts as a confirmed overlap only when it clears one of two gold standards; everything weaker is dropped: high : identical full day+month+year of birth + compatible names medium : VÚA `note_legion` is True + same birth okres + same birth year + compatible names — the Poznámka **explicitly** records Legion service and the demographics pin which legionnaire. Four refusals sit on top (v1.3.0): a pair whose full dates of birth both exist and disagree is refused — it is direct evidence against identity, and 31 note-confirmed pairs used to carry one; a surname scoring 85-90 counts only when the birth okres agrees too; one-to-one : each legion id keeps its best candidate and each VÚA id its best claimant; a tie at the top is refused rather than broken by lookup order; criterion B only fires on the corrected note_legion ( habsburg 1.2.0), which no longer mistakes the interwar army's register references for Legion service. Known recall limitations (deliberate — state in the paper's linkage appendix): both criteria require an exact birth year; a person can only DOB-confirm when both sides carry a full (not year-only) birth date; exact ties are refused, so a man recorded twice in csol (see add_duplicate_groups ) cannot link at all. This sheet shows each such pair as the page prints it — a row per pair, each token labelled and cut from real pages — so the reader can decide by the difference instead of by the name. Which pairs. Every pair the readers swapped at least PAIR_MIN times against the gold, counted over all r5 passes on the pages of --roles ( e3_verdicts_r5.csv : a reader's token on a box the gold names otherwise), at most MAX_PAIRS , most swapped first. Which cuts. Up to CUTS per token, from different scans where it can: the glyphs the author clicked for test A first ( output/glyph_bank ), then E3's alignment of the gold ( boxes_gold.csv ) — but an aligned box only where DINOv3, the encoder of record classifying it leave-page-out, names the gold's token on it ( e3_predictions.csv ). TL;DR Pair every Czech page of the 1910 register with the German pages that print it. 1910 register · v1.0.0 · 341 lines · 11 public functions · 7 constants · used by nothing else · utils/lexikon_1910/build_de_page_map.py normalise parse_head court_crosswalk de_page_words de_page_courts load_de_volume cz_page_names match_page build report main ROOT GRID_CSV GRID_VOLUME OUT_CSV MIN_NAME WEAK_BELOW FIELDS How it works The two volumes are the same census table set twice, and neither is a translation of the other's typesetting: they paginate differently and each orders an okres's municipalities alphabetically in its own language . So there is no scan-to-scan correspondence to assume — German scan 118 is not the German printing of Czech scan 118 — and a run that assumes one reads unrelated pages while looking entirely well-behaved. What makes the pairing possible is that both volumes print both names. The Czech table sets Vysoká, Wisset ; the German sets Wisset, Vysoká . So the German twin of every municipality on a Czech page can be read straight off the Czech page, and the German page that prints those same names is the page that covers it. No external crosswalk, no district-name translation table, and — this is the point — the match score is itself the evidence . A bad pairing shows up as a low score rather than as a clean-looking wrong answer. Two guards, both from failures measured in this project: The district is checked first. Village names repeat across Bohemia, and a name-only match over 481 pages will find a homonym in another okres. Candidate pages are therefore restricted to those whose running head names the right politischer Bezirk before names are counted — the same discipline records_geo uses when a birthplace could be one of several places. A tie is refused, not broken. Where two DE pages score equally the row is written ambiguous and carries both. lexikon_1910_de already refuses a tie one level down rather than taking the first match, and for the same reason: on this source a plausible wrong answer is indistinguishable from a right one. Output — reference/places/lexikon_1910_de_page_map.csv : cz_scan de_scans score n_names n_matched districts_cz verdict verdict is matched / weak / ambiguous / unmatched . So this script does the expensive half once and writes small tracked artifacts under reference/places/figure/ : a handful of JPEGs and one JSON file holding every overlay box, every verbatim string the box covers, and the pilot's headline counts. build_docs.py then only reads that. Every box is computed, never eyeballed. The Czech page has an ALTO layer whose frame is the scan's own pixel grid, so utils.lexikon_1910.lexikon_1910.render_page renders it 1:1 and the module's existing geometry — body_band , fit_columns , segment_blocks , notes_boxes , the per-line bounds extract_notes already returns — lands directly on the image with no scale factor to carry around. Boxes are then divided by the image size, so the figure survives any later change of render width. The German side is coarser and says so. The UBW scan has no ALTO and no printed rules — page.rects and page.lines are empty — so its boxes come from pdfplumber word extents clustered into printed lines. That is enough for the one point the German page is on the sheet to make (the same municipality, a different page and a different position in the district, because each edition sorts an okres alphabetically in its own language), and not enough to draw a column grid on. Run it from the repo root:: python utils/lexikon_1910/build_lexikon_figure.py Nothing here calls a paid API or a model. It reads two PDFs, one ALTO file, the symbol atlas manifest and — if the pilot has been run — the pilot's check CSVs. Functions class Zone One clickable region of a page, in fractions of the image. Ш katastrální (berní) obec. + pohodný. ;šľ spořitelna. Until now the vision channel was handed an English word list — [school] primary school — and asked to map a 1916 printed glyph onto it. It had never seen this typeface's symbols, so it matched on resemblance, which is why two readers given the identical mark returned [doctor] and [rc-curate] . This script replaces the word list with the printed forms themselves. The plate is self-labelling, which is what makes this mostly mechanical. The OCR destroys every symbol on it ( ® , Ш , <3* , € , tí ) and reads every gloss cleanly — and those glosses are already the expansion column of institution_abbreviations.csv . So the gloss says which token the symbol is, and the plate's own geometry says where the symbol is: each column is a narrow band of pictograms, a blank gutter, then the meanings, so the widest block of ink in a column is the gloss and everything left of it is the picture. Taking the crop boundary from the layout rather than from the symbol's own characters is what makes it work on the lines where the OCR emitted nothing for the symbol at all. What comes out symbols/<token>.png one crop per pictogram, at scan resolution symbols/manifest.csv token, printed gloss, match score, source box symbols/atlas.png the crops with their tokens beside them, as one image — this is what a vision model can be shown And a report of the three ways the plate and the curated table disagree, which is the other thing this buys. A plate line that matches no token means the token list is incomplete and any such symbol on a page comes back [?] however good the reader is; the plate prints turistická bouda , salaš, koliha and klášterec , none of which the table currently carries. A token with no plate line means it was inferred rather than read off the legend. Until now the vision channel was handed an **English word list** — ``[school] primary school`` — and asked to map a 1916 printed glyph onto it. It had never seen this typeface's symbols, so it matched on resemblance, which is why two readers given the identical mark returned ``[doctor]`` and ``[rc-curate]``. This script replaces the word list with the printed forms themselves. **The plate is self-labelling, which is what makes this mostly mechanical.** The OCR destroys every symbol on it (``®``, ``Ш``, ``<3*``, ``€``, ``tí``) and reads every *gloss* cleanly — and those glosses are already the ``expansion`` column of ``institution_abbreviations.csv``. So the gloss says which token the symbol is, and the plate's own geometry says where the symbol is: each column is a narrow band of pictograms, a blank gutter, then the meanings, so the widest block of ink in a column *is* the gloss and everything left of it is the picture. Taking the crop boundary from the layout rather than from the symbol's own characters is what makes it work on the lines where the OCR emitted nothing for the symbol at all. What comes out -------------- ``symbols/<token>.png`` one crop per pictogram, at scan resolution ``symbols/manifest.csv`` token, printed gloss, match score, source box ``symbols/atlas.png`` the crops with their tokens beside them, as one image — this is what a vision model can be shown And a report of the three ways the plate and the curated table disagree, which is the other thing this buys. The Spezialortsrepertorium von Böhmen explains its pictograms on the plate Zeichenerklärung , p. XI — scan 0012 of the UBW scan — three columns wide, one symbol to a line with its German meaning beside it, exactly as the Czech Výklad značek does on its p. XI. The German reader is shown its own volume's plate, not the Czech one. The two plates are not the same list: the German one prints 80 symbols, and the three the Czech plate has beyond them — [cooperative] , [port] and [rc-parish-exp] — are not on it (the German volume writes cooperatives as letters only, and a parish expositure as the word Exp. ). The prompt tells the reader that the key "is the whole of what this volume prints", so a Czech key would be a false statement to a German reader, three times over. How it works is the Czech builder's, reused rather than copied: the plate is self-labelling, so each printed gloss names its token through the de pictogram rows of institution_abbreviations.csv (whose expansions were read off this same plate), and the layout — symbol band, gutter, gloss — gives the crop. The one difference is the text layer: this PDF has no ALTO, so the words come from the PDF's own positional OCR layer ( pymupdf get_text("words") ), scaled onto a render at the Czech plate's width so the Czech builder's pixel constants keep their meaning. This script gathers every such token, cuts the lines of the scan it came from, ranks the atlas tokens it most resembles, and writes a queue the Token Review artifact page reads. This module reconstructs that table from the NDK ALTO layer of the Czech volume and grades the result against the arithmetic the table itself must satisfy. Three facts about the source do the structural work, and none of them depend on reading a character correctly: The printed rules are in the ALTO. GraphicalElement entries taller than they are wide are the column rules; the tall ones bound the table body. Column boundaries are therefore measured, not inferred from a text histogram. The area column is printed only on municipality rows. That is the block delimiter — typography is not usable here, because the NDK TextStyle entries are synthetic (Times New Roman, sizes 5–10) and carry no weight. Column 1 runs two interleaved integer sequences — municipalities incrementing across the okres, osady restarting at 1 inside each. The OCR mangles them ( o , í) , Г) o ), but the sequence is known a priori, so row identity is reconstructed rather than read. The invariants in INVARIANTS are the grader. They are deliberately kept out of the transcription prompt (see run_lexikon_1910_pilot.py ): a model told what the numbers must add up to will produce numbers that add up. Column labels are provisional — the groupings the invariants use are certain (they are what the rules enclose), but the label on columns 9/10 in particular is read off the header and awaits confirmation against the preface, pp. VIII–XIV. They are strong, but they share one blind spot: they cannot see a municipality the parser never emitted, or a block it invented. An okres that is missing three villages satisfies every one of them, because each surviving row is individually consistent. Nothing inside the page can detect a row that is not on it. This module closes that gap by summing the transcribed municipality rows across a whole okres and comparing the totals to census_okres_1910 , which reports the same 1910 enumeration at okres level from the Rumpler-Seger workbooks. Where the two disagree, either the transcription lost or duplicated a row, or the confession grouping below is wrong — and the two are told apart by how they disagree: a lost row is a deficit in every column at once, a bad grouping is an exact offset in one. This is not independent evidence about 1910. Both sides descend from the same census, so agreement validates our reading of the register, not the register itself. That is exactly what is wanted here, but it means the reconciliation must never be cited as corroboration of the census. Two things about the comparison need stating rather than assuming: Only municipality rows are summed. Settlements are subdivisions of their municipality and are already counted in it — the same double-count that invariant I4 exists to check. Summing both would inflate every total by roughly a factor of two and would do it consistently , which is the kind of error that looks like a result. It needs a complete okres. A partial okres under-sums by construction, so a run that covers half a district would report a spurious deficit in every column. Coverage is therefore a precondition, checked against the anchoring, not a caveat in the output. Functions def is_summary_row ( row ) -> bool Is this a district aggregate rather than a municipality? It stays as a guard for callers that assemble blocks some other way — a summary row reaching a sum adds a whole district back into itself, which cost a factor of four on okres Kraslice before it was caught, and that is worth one cheap check. What none of them settles stays unresolved: a court is never guessed. Among a page's few names a match needs five letters — the German Tepl (Teplá) begins Teplice-Šanov — and the best of several must lead the next by ten points. Twin courts. The backbone carries Liberec twice: the rural court (okres Liberec) and the statutory city's (okres Liberec (město)). Statistische Zentralkommission's Prague office, once in German. Neither is a translation of the other's typesetting — the two volumes are ordered differently (Czech by Czech district name, German by German), paginate differently, and were composited and proofed separately. Disagreement between them therefore flags an error with no human in the loop, which is as close to free double-keying as a source like this ever gets. Two things make the German side harder than the Czech one, and both are handled here rather than assumed away: No ALTO and no printed rules. The UBW scan carries an embedded text layer but page.rects and page.lines are empty, so the grid has to come from the words themselves. The numeric columns are right-aligned, so their right edges pile up into sharp peaks — the same right-edge read lexikon_sk.py uses for the Slovak lexicon. The scans are not consistently cropped (511–541 pt wide across a sample of 80 pages), so absolute positions smear into unusable bands. Normalising each page against its own text extent resolves them back into peaks. The volumes are located against each other through the running head, which prints Politischer Bezirk: Gerichtsbezirk , and then matched by name within an okres. Not by the printed running number: each volume orders an okres's municipalities alphabetically in its own language, so the same place carries a different number in each — a join on the number pairs unrelated municipalities while looking entirely well-behaved. Read by two readers, they are two error-prone measurements of one binary fact — municipality m has institution c — and the two-measure identification of a misclassified regressor (Kane, Rouse and Staiger; Black, Berger and Scott) needs the two errors to be independent given the truth . D-58 makes the German edition a second measurement only if that holds on the gold; this module is the test. The pairing is by court and municipality name, never by page (D-67). Each edition numbers a court's municipalities in its own alphabetical order, so municipality 23 of Trutnov in Czech is 1 in German, and the municipalities of one Czech page fall on two or three German scans. A municipality is paired when its two printed names share a form — Pilníkov, Pilnikau and Pilnikau, Pilnikov — inside the same court, one to one, and a name that would pair with two municipalities is refused rather than given to either. The unit is the municipality, not the settlement. Parts are numbered within a municipality in the edition's own order too, and the two editions do not always split a municipality into the same parts, so a settlement-level pairing would be a second name join on worse names. Claims are pooled over a municipality's parts and pages on both sides. The truth is each edition's own gold. A claim both golds make is a positive , a claim neither makes but some reader does is a negative , and a claim only one gold makes is an edition disagreement — a difference between the two prints, or a slip of the transcriber's — which is listed and kept out of the test, since neither reader can be wrong about it in the same sense. The test, for a Czech pass A and a German pass B, inside each truth class: the joint errors J = Σ e_A · e_B against what independence predicts, with a permutation p-value from shuffling B's errors (Dell and Rambachan's check). It is run twice — permuting within the truth class, and within (truth class, symbol) . The second is the one that matters: two readers who both find one glyph hard err together on it while erring independently given the glyph, and pooling over glyphs reads that as dependence. A pair passes D-58 only on the second; the first is printed beside it so the size of the glyph effect shows. Read by two readers, they are two error-prone measurements of one binary fact — *municipality m has institution c* — and the two-measure identification of a misclassified regressor (Kane, Rouse and Staiger; Black, Berger and Scott) needs the two errors to be **independent given the truth**.
