script-utils-parsing-occupations: TL;DR The raw field is Czech free text: 119,046 non-empty values over 8,004 distinct strings, 7,169 after normalisation. It is heavily concentrated — rolník alone is 21,457 records, the top 200 normalised keys are 88.1 % and the top 1,000 are 93.9 % — so a curated dictionary is tractable where a general Czech occupational parser would not be. Output & support · v1.4.0 · 728 lines · 9 public functions · 8 constants · used by 02_data_cleaning.ipynb , 03_visualisation.ipynb , utils/parsing/schema.py +7 · utils/parsing/occupations.py load_hisco_authority load_occupation_curation split_occupations extract_qualifier extract_career_stage code_occupation add_occupation_columns matcher_selftest occupation_report ROOT AUTHORITY_CSV CURATION_CSV ADJECTIVE_KEYS CAREER_STAGE CAREER_STAGE_ORD ABBREV ABBREV_CONTEXT How it works The Czech step has to be authored. Neither the History of Work title dictionary (whose lang_code covers FR/NL/DE/EN/SV and others) nor OccCANINE (13 languages) has Czech. What the external sources do supply, and this module uses, is everything downstream of the code: reference/occupations/hisco_authority.csv turns a HISCO code plus its status / relation / product modifiers into an English label, HISCLASS, HISCLASS_5, HISCAM and SOCPO. Matching is exact on the normalised key , never substring. That is deliberate: the two defects the 2026-07 audit found in this repo were an unanchored substring match ( generálmajor scoring as major ) and missing values fabricating content. Compounds are handled by splitting on token boundaries into curated keys — never by testing whether one key occurs inside another string. Compounds get one of three token-boundary treatments, and which one fired is recorded in occupation_match so any analysis can restrict to whatever it trusts: exact the whole normalised string is a curated key (~93.9 %) dual it splits cleanly into two curated keys — `rolník zámečník`, `rolník a obuvník`. Both are coded: the first into the primary columns (the HISCO convention, and what HSN's DOUBLE table does), the second into the `*_2` columns. A man who farms his fields and does a trade for extra money is both, and which one matters is an analytical choice made downstream, not here. head an adjective and a curated head noun — `mlynářský dělník`, `tovární dozorce`. The head noun carries the code. prefix a curated key followed by something uncurated — the key carries it. none unmatched; every output column stays <NA> Two guards keep the compound rules from inventing a class. ADJECTIVE_KEYS (below) stops a curated key that is really a qualifier from hijacking the compound as its primary. And where the qualifier changes the trade rather than its object — akademický malíř is a fine artist, not a house painter — the whole string is curated in occupation_hisco_curation.csv so it matches exact and never reaches these rules at all. Decomposition is the default, not the answer to everything. The qualifier is kept, not discarded (v1.2.0). strojní zámečník and zámečník are different jobs and desert at different rates (Russia: 3.38 % vs 6.06 % on the 2026-08-27 build; OCCUPATION_CODING.md §4 carries the live figures), so the modifier is extracted into its own column by extract_qualifier — deliberately independently of the match kind , by locating the curated head noun inside the string. Keying it off the match kind instead would have thrown the qualifier away again the moment a compound was promoted to a curated exact key, which is exactly what this release does to the high-volume ones. dual is the one kind excluded: in rolník zámečník the leading token is a second occupation, not a modifier, and it is already coded in the *_2 columns. CAREER_STAGE extracts the other axis the strings carry — mistr , učeň , adjunkt , příručí , majitel . HISCO's own status modifier is populated on only ~2.7 % of coded records because csol.cz simply does not record employment status; the token scan reaches ~3.7 k. It is descriptive: it never touches hisco or the class. HISCAM was removed in v1.2.0 — see reference/DECISIONS.md D-30. It is non-monotonic on this sample, and the one thing it was still buying (separating zámečník 60 from strojní zámečník 66) is now carried explicitly by the qualifier column instead. 715 716 717 718 719 720 721 722 723 724 725 726 727 728 """ occupations.py — HISCO / HISCLASS coding of the free-text ``Zaměstnání`` field ============================================================================== The raw field is Czech free text: 119,046 non-empty values over 8,004 distinct strings, 7,169 after normalisation. It is heavily concentrated — ``rolník`` alone is 21,457 records, the top 200 normalised keys are 88.1 % and the top 1,000 are 93.9 % — so a curated dictionary is tractable where a general Czech occupational parser would not be. **The Czech step has to be authored.** Neither the History of Work title dictionary (whose ``lang_code`` covers FR/NL/DE/EN/SV and others) nor OccCANINE (13 languages) has Czech. What the external sources do supply, and this module uses, is everything downstream of the code: ``reference/occupations/hisco_authority.csv`` turns a HISCO code plus its status / relation / product modifiers into an English label, HISCLASS, HISCLASS_5, HISCAM and SOCPO. Matching is **exact on the normalised key**, never substring. That is deliberate: the two defects the 2026-07 audit found in this repo were an unanchored substring match (``generálmajor`` scoring as ``major``) and missing values fabricating content. Compounds are handled by splitting on token boundaries into curated keys — never by testing whether one key occurs inside another string. Compounds get one of three token-boundary treatments, and which one fired is recorded in ``occupation_match`` so any analysis can restrict to whatever it trusts: exact the whole normalised string is a curated key (~93.9 %) dual it splits cleanly into two curated keys — ``rolník zámečník``, ``rolník a obuvník``. Both are coded: the first into the primary columns (the HISCO convention, and what HSN's DOUBLE table does), the second into the ``*_2`` columns. A man who farms his fields and does a trade for extra money is both, and which one matters is an analytical choice made downstream, not here. head an adjective and a curated head noun — ``mlynářský dělník``, ``tovární dozorce``. The head noun carries the code. prefix a curated key followed by something uncurated — the key carries it. none unmatched; every output column stays <NA> Two guards keep the compound rules from inventing a class. ``ADJECTIVE_KEYS`` (below) stops a curated key that is really a qualifier from hijacking the compound as its primary. And where the qualifier changes the *trade* rather than its object — ``akademický malíř`` is a fine artist, not a house painter — the whole string is curated in ``occupation_hisco_curation.csv`` so it matches ``exact`` and never reaches these rules at all. Decomposition is the default, not the answer to everything. **The qualifier is kept, not discarded** (v1.2.0). ``strojní zámečník`` and ``zámečník`` are different jobs and desert at different rates (Russia: 3.38 % vs 6.06 % on the 2026-08-27 build; ``OCCUPATION_CODING.md`` §4 carries the live figures), so the modifier is extracted into its own column by ``extract_qualifier`` — deliberately *independently of the match kind*, by locating the curated head noun inside the string. Keying it off the match kind instead would have thrown the qualifier away again the moment a compound was promoted to a curated ``exact`` key, which is exactly what this release does to the high-volume ones. ``dual`` is the one kind excluded: in ``rolník zámečník`` the leading token is a second occupation, not a modifier, and it is already coded in the ``*_2`` columns. ``CAREER_STAGE`` extracts the other axis the strings carry — ``mistr``, ``učeň``, ``adjunkt``, ``příručí``, ``majitel``. HISCO's own status modifier is populated on only ~2.7 % of coded records because csol.cz simply does not record employment status; the token scan reaches ~3.7 k. It is descriptive: it never touches ``hisco`` or the class. HISCAM was removed in v1.2.0 — see ``reference/DECISIONS.md`` D-30. It is non-monotonic on this sample, and the one thing it was still buying (separating ``zámečník`` 60 from ``strojní zámečník`` 66) is now carried explicitly by the qualifier column instead. script-utils-scraping-scraper_kramerius: TL;DR Kramerius v5 downloader — importable module + CLI. Output & support · v1.4.0 · 638 lines · 6 public functions · 6 constants · used by utils/scraping/run_lexicon_downloads.py , utils/scraping/run_oeulk_downloads.py · utils/scraping/scraper_kramerius.py KrameriusClient parse_pid parse_host safe_filename download_document main DEFAULT_HOST API_PATH USER_AGENT PAGE_MODEL CONTAINER_MODELS INTERNAL_PART_MODELS How it works Downloads a whole digital-library document (all its pages) from a Kramerius 5 instance as a single PDF (the page scans) plus a concatenated TXT (the per-page OCR). Written for the Digitální studovna Ministerstva obrany ČR (DSMO) — the Czech Ministry-of-Defence Kramerius that hosts the front diaries (deníky) and the Austro-Hungarian Schematismus volumes — but it works against any public Kramerius 5.x host (National Library, MZK, …); just pass --host . What a Kramerius document looks like Every object has a pid ( uuid:XX… ) and a model . Container models ( periodical , periodicalvolume , periodicalitem , monograph , monographunit , convolute …) hold ordered children; leaf pages have model == "page" . This downloader walks that tree from any starting pid and collects the page pids in document order , so you can hand it either a whole periodical or a single issue. A third kind of child is neither: an internal part ( picture for a map or plate, internalpart for a chapter heading) labels pages that already hang off the same parent, and its own /children hands those pages back a second time. The walk skips them — the Beilagen volumes of Österreich-Ungarns letzter Krieg list 84 picture maps beside 88 pages, and recursing into the maps nearly doubled the volume. Per-page datastreams used (confirmed present on DSMO): IMG_FULL image/jpeg full-resolution page scan -> PDF TEXT_OCR text/plain OCR of that page -> TXT ALTO text/xml (word coordinates; optional, --alto) API shape (v5.0), relative to {host}/search/api/v5.0 : /item/{pid} -> {pid, model, title, root_title, details, …} /item/{pid}/children -> [ {pid, model, title/label, …}, … ] (ordered) /item/{pid}/streams/IMG_FULL -> bytes (jpeg) /item/{pid}/streams/TEXT_OCR -> text /item/{pid}/streams/ALTO -> xml Scan resolution IMG_FULL is not the scan. DSMO serves it scaled to 1500 px wide , while the image server behind the viewer holds the page at its native size — 2370 px for a map sheet of Österreich-Ungarns letzter Krieg , about 2000 px for a text page. native_images=True ( --native-images ) fetches that instead, from the host's IIIF endpoint (outside the v5 API path): {host}/search/iiif/{pid}/full/full/0/default.jpg -> bytes (jpeg), native size Off by default, because not every Kramerius 5 host runs an image server; a page the endpoint will not serve falls back to IMG_FULL with a warning. Access note Only pages whose access policy is public can be fetched in full; licensed / DNNT pages return 403 for IMG_FULL. Such pages are logged and (with --fallback-preview ) substituted by the lower-res IMG_PREVIEW so the PDF stays complete. The DSMO Schematismus / pre-1920 diaries are public domain. PDF assembly uses img2pdf when available (lossless — the original JPEGs are embedded as-is); otherwise it falls back to Pillow (re-encodes). Install img2pdf for faithful, smaller output. Progress is shown as a tqdm bar over the page loop ( --no-progress , or progress=False , falls back to a log line every 25 pages). Several documents can share one screen by giving each a progress_position — see run_lexicon_downloads.py . Downloads a whole digital-library document (all its pages) from a Kramerius 5 instance as a single **PDF** (the page scans) plus a concatenated **TXT** (the per-page OCR). Written for the *Digitální studovna Ministerstva obrany ČR* (DSMO) — the Czech Ministry-of-Defence Kramerius that hosts the front diaries (deníky) and the Austro-Hungarian *Schematismus* volumes — but it works against any public Kramerius 5.x host (National Library, MZK, …); just pass ``--host``. What a Kramerius document looks like ------------------------------------ Every object has a ``pid`` (``uuid:XX…``) and a ``model``. Container models (``periodical``, ``periodicalvolume``, ``periodicalitem``, ``monograph``, ``monographunit``, ``convolute``…) hold ordered children; leaf pages have ``model == "page"``. This downloader walks that tree from any starting pid and collects the page pids **in document order**, so you can hand it either a whole periodical or a single issue. A third kind of child is neither: an *internal part* (``picture`` for a map or plate, ``internalpart`` for a chapter heading) labels pages that already hang off the same parent, and its own ``/children`` hands those pages back a second time. The walk skips them — the *Beilagen* volumes of *Österreich-Ungarns letzter Krieg* list 84 ``picture`` maps beside 88 pages, and recursing into the maps nearly doubled the volume. Per-page datastreams used (confirmed present on DSMO): IMG_FULL image/jpeg full-resolution page scan -> PDF TEXT_OCR text/plain OCR of that page -> TXT ALTO text/xml (word coordinates; optional, --alto) API shape (v5.0), relative to ``{host}/search/api/v5.0``: /item/{pid} -> {pid, model, title, root_title, details, …} /item/{pid}/children -> [ {pid, model, title/label, …}, … ] (ordered) /item/{pid}/streams/IMG_FULL -> bytes (jpeg) /item/{pid}/streams/TEXT_OCR -> text /item/{pid}/streams/ALTO -> xml Scan resolution --------------- ``IMG_FULL`` is not the scan. DSMO serves it scaled to **1500 px wide**, while the image server behind the viewer holds the page at its native size — 2370 px for a map sheet of *Österreich-Ungarns letzter Krieg*, about 2000 px for a text page. ``native_images=True`` (``--native-images``) fetches that instead, from the host's IIIF endpoint (outside the v5 API path): {host}/search/iiif/{pid}/full/full/0/default.jpg -> bytes (jpeg), native size Off by default, because not every Kramerius 5 host runs an image server; a page the endpoint will not serve falls back to ``IMG_FULL`` with a warning. Access note ----------- Only pages whose access ``policy`` is ``public`` can be fetched in full; licensed / DNNT pages return 403 for IMG_FULL. Such pages are logged and (with ``--fallback-preview``) substituted by the lower-res IMG_PREVIEW so the PDF stays complete. The DSMO *Schematismus* / pre-1920 diaries are public domain. PDF assembly uses ``img2pdf`` when available (lossless — the original JPEGs are embedded as-is); otherwise it falls back to Pillow (re-encodes). Install ``img2pdf`` for faithful, smaller output. Progress is shown as a ``tqdm`` bar over the page loop (``--no-progress``, or ``progress=False``, falls back to a log line every 25 pages). Several documents can share one screen by giving each a ``progress_position`` — see ``run_lexicon_downloads.py``. Output & support · v1.2.0 · 601 lines · 6 public functions · 4 constants · used by utils/scraping/run_lexicon_downloads.py · utils/scraping/scraper_kramerius7.py Kramerius7Client parse_pid parse_host safe_filename download_document main DEFAULT_HOST API_PATH USER_AGENT PAGE_MODEL How it works Downloads a whole digital-library document (all its pages) from a Kramerius 7 instance as a single PDF (the page scans), a concatenated TXT (the per-page OCR) and, where present, per-page ALTO XML (word coordinates). Written for the Moravskoslezská vědecká knihovna (MSVK, kramerius.msvk.cz ) but should work against any Kramerius 7.x "client v7.0" REST API; just pass --host . Why this is a separate module from scraper_kramerius.py That module targets Kramerius v5 ( /search/api/v5.0/item/{pid}/... , streams/IMG_FULL datastream names). Kramerius v7 renamed almost everything: a different base path, JSON-only responses shaped differently, no children endpoint (404), and per-page datastreams that hang off /items/{pid}/image and /items/{pid}/ocr/... instead of a generic streams/{NAME} . The two APIs are incompatible enough that patching one module to handle both would obscure more than it saved, so this is a fresh, parallel implementation that mirrors the v5 module's conventions (docstring shape, __version__ , client class, download_document() entry point, argparse CLI, resumable page cache, PDF assembly) so the two scrapers stay interchangeable from the caller's point of view. What a Kramerius 7 document looks like Every object has a pid ( uuid:XX… ) and a model . A monograph (or periodical / periodicalvolume / periodicalitem / monographunit ) holds page children directly; leaf pages have model == "page" . Kramerius 7 also has an internalpart model (chapter/section headings such as "Vorwort") that hangs off the same parent via hasIntCompPart but does not introduce further pages of its own — it just labels a range of the same pages via a foster isOnPage relation — so it is ignored when collecting the page list. Why this is a separate module from ``scraper_kramerius.py`` ------------------------------------------------------------- That module targets Kramerius **v5** (``/search/api/v5.0/item/{pid}/...``, ``streams/IMG_FULL`` datastream names). Kramerius **v7** renamed almost everything: a different base path, JSON-only responses shaped differently, no ``children`` endpoint (404), and per-page datastreams that hang off ``/items/{pid}/image`` and ``/items/{pid}/ocr/...`` instead of a generic ``streams/{NAME}``. The two APIs are incompatible enough that patching one module to handle both would obscure more than it saved, so this is a fresh, parallel implementation that mirrors the v5 module's *conventions* (docstring shape, ``__version__``, client class, ``download_document()`` entry point, argparse CLI, resumable page cache, PDF assembly) so the two scrapers stay interchangeable from the caller's point of view. What a Kramerius 7 document looks like --------------------------------------- Every object has a ``pid`` (``uuid:XX…``) and a ``model``. A ``monograph`` (or ``periodical`` / ``periodicalvolume`` / ``periodicalitem`` / ``monographunit``) holds page children directly; leaf pages have ``model == "page"``. Kramerius 7 also has an ``internalpart`` model (chapter/section headings such as "Vorwort") that hangs off the same parent via ``hasIntCompPart`` but does **not** introduce further pages of its own — it just labels a range of the same pages via a foster ``isOnPage`` relation — so it is ignored when collecting the page list. Two ways to enumerate the pages were probed against this host; both work and return an identical, sort-index-ordered page list, so this module uses whichever the caller does not override: /search/api/client/v7.0/items/{pid}/info/structure -> {"children": {"own": [{"pid", "relation": "hasPage"|"hasIntCompPart"}, ...]}} Filter to ``relation == "hasPage"``; the array order already matches document order (verified against ``page.index`` below). /search/api/client/v7.0/search ?q=own_parent.pid:"{pid}" AND model:page &rows=2000&sort=rels_ext_index.sort asc &fl=pid,model,title.search,page.index,page.number -> {"response": {"docs": [{"pid", "page.index", "page.number", ...}, ...]}} Explicitly sorted by the Fedora RELS-EXT ordering predicate; carries the printed page number/label for free. This is what the module uses by default (``iter_pages``), falling back to ``info/structure`` if the Solr query ever comes back empty. ``/search/api/client/v7.0/items/{pid}/children`` (the v5-shaped guess) is a straight 404 on this host — do not use it. Per-document metadata / access info: /search/api/client/v7.0/items/{pid}/info -> {"providedByLicenses": [...], "data": {"image": {...}, "ocr": {...}}, ...} Access-policy summary (e.g. "public"), not a display title. /search/api/client/v7.0/search?q=pid:"{pid}"&fl=pid,model,title.search, title.sort,date.str,root.pid,root.title -> the actual bibliographic title, root title, model and date. Used for the identity check and the output filename. /search/api/client/v7.0/items/{pid}/info/data -> {"image": {"preview","thumb","full"}, "ocr": {"text","alto"}, ...} Per-item boolean availability flags — checked once per page so a genuinely-absent stream is skipped without wasting a 404 round-trip (Kramerius 7 answers a missing datastream with 404, not an empty body). Per-page datastreams (confirmed present on kramerius.msvk.cz, 2026-08): /items/{pid}/image image/jpeg full-resolution page scan -> PDF /items/{pid}/ocr/text text/plain OCR of that page -> TXT /items/{pid}/ocr/alto text/xml ALTO word coordinates -> per-page XML (if present) Progress -------- A ``tqdm`` bar is drawn over the page loop (``--no-progress``, or ``progress=False``, falls back to a log line every 25 pages). Several documents can share one screen by giving each a ``progress_position`` — see ``run_lexicon_downloads.py``. TLS note -------- ``requests`` fails certificate verification against this host even though the Windows trust store (and curl) accept it — the local certifi bundle is stale for this host's chain. Default here is therefore ``verify_tls=False`` (the opposite default from the v5 module, which talks to a host that verifies fine); pass ``--verify-tls`` to force verification back on. TL;DR Verlustlisten Österreich-Ungarns 1914–1919 (DES index) scraper — importable module + CLI. Output & support · v0.1.0 · 743 lines · 19 public functions · 27 constants · used by 01_data_collection.ipynb · utils/scraping/scraper_verlustlisten.py BlockedError ServerUnhealthyError RequestBudgetExceeded CanaryError project_of parse_record make_session DESClient read_ledger write_source_note walk_ids check_canary scrape_range pilot_ids run_pilot pilot_report test_id build_parser main BASE_URL RECORD_URL PROJECT_SLUG PROJECT_TITLE EXPECTED_ENTRIES EXPECTED_PAGES CITATION ID_LOW ID_HIGH CANARY_ID CANARY FIELD_MAP FIELD_COLUMNS RECORD_COLUMNS LEDGER_COLUMNS MIN_DELAY DEFAULT_DELAY MAX_ADAPTIVE_DELAY RETRY_STATUS MAX_BACKOFF DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE DEFAULT_BATCH_PAUSE PILOT_BANDS USER_AGENT ROOT DEFAULT_OUT_DIR PILOT_OUT_DIR How it works Feasibility pilot first. The index of the k.u.k. casualty lists, transcribed by volunteers of the Verein für Computergenealogie (CompGen), Familia Austria and partners (the VHÚ Praha among them), is served by CompGen's Data Entry System (DES) as project ou1wk . Statistics page, 2026-10-15: 2,694,074 entries on 36,850 list pages , every page "confirmed complete" since 2022-01-16. How the site can be read — and why that sets the cost Each entry has one server-rendered page, /search/show/{record_id} , with no login. robots.txt disallows only /search/suggest/ (checked 2026-10-15). The project search returns no result list without a login , and the global search returns name + UUID only. Neither is used: this module never logs in. record_id is one integer space shared by every DES project (address books, civil registers, the German casualty lists …). ou1wk entries sit roughly between IDs 13 M and 21 M, interleaved with other projects; an unused ID answers 302 to the home page. So a complete read is a walk over every ID in that band, and its cost is set by how densely ou1wk fills it — which is what the pilot measures. The pilot ( run_pilot ) fetches a seeded, stratified random sample of IDs across the band plus a few short consecutive windows, and pilot_report turns that into (a) the ou1wk share by ID band and an estimate of requests and days for a full walk, (b) run lengths inside the windows (whether skipping foreign blocks could ever pay), (c) per-field fill rates and status values on a random sample of entries. Fields of one entry Page Number ( {Ausgabe}_{page} ), Ausgabe , Datum (date of the list), Last name , First name , Offizier/Mannschaft , Charge , Truppenkörper , Unterabteilung , Land , Bezirk , Heimatort , Geburtsjahr , Status , Ereignisdatum , Ort/Region/Land des Ereignisses — plus the entry's UUID (the only identifier CompGen asks to be cited) and the link to the page scan. Values are stored verbatim; a field the page does not know is kept in extra_fields (JSON), never dropped. Politeness — and identity Sequential, one connection, never parallel; delay below MIN_DELAY is refused; the pause stretches to twice the server's last response time; a rest of batch_pause s every batch_size requests. Backs off on 429/5xx (honouring Retry-After ), stops after a run of consecutive failures ( ServerUnhealthyError ), and stops at once on a bot challenge or a login redirect ( BlockedError ) — neither is worked around. Every probed ID goes to ledger.csv and is never requested twice; re-runs resume. No identity is sent. The User-Agent names this script and its version only; the session refuses all cookies (the server hands out a JSESSIONID on every response), so requests carry no session either. Statistics page, 2026-10-15: **2,694,074 entries on 36,850 list pages**, every page "confirmed complete" since 2022-01-16. How the site can be read — and why that sets the cost ----------------------------------------------------- * Each entry has one server-rendered page, ``/search/show/{record_id}``, with no login. ``robots.txt`` disallows only ``/search/suggest/`` (checked 2026-10-15). * The **project search returns no result list without a login**, and the global search returns name + UUID only. Neither is used: this module never logs in. * ``record_id`` is **one integer space shared by every DES project** (address books, civil registers, the German casualty lists …). ``ou1wk`` entries sit roughly between IDs 13 M and 21 M, interleaved with other projects; an unused ID answers ``302`` to the home page. So a complete read is a walk over every ID in that band, and its cost is set by how densely ``ou1wk`` fills it — which is what the pilot measures. The pilot (:func:`run_pilot`) fetches a seeded, stratified random sample of IDs across the band plus a few short consecutive windows, and :func:`pilot_report` turns that into (a) the ``ou1wk`` share by ID band and an estimate of requests and days for a full walk, (b) run lengths inside the windows (whether skipping foreign blocks could ever pay), (c) per-field fill rates and status values on a random sample of entries. Fields of one entry ------------------- ``Page Number`` (``{Ausgabe}_{page}``), ``Ausgabe``, ``Datum`` (date of the list), ``Last name``, ``First name``, ``Offizier/Mannschaft``, ``Charge``, ``Truppenkörper``, ``Unterabteilung``, ``Land``, ``Bezirk``, ``Heimatort``, ``Geburtsjahr``, ``Status``, ``Ereignisdatum``, ``Ort/Region/Land des Ereignisses`` — plus the entry's UUID (the only identifier CompGen asks to be cited) and the link to the page scan. Values are stored verbatim; a field the page does not know is kept in ``extra_fields`` (JSON), never dropped. All named constants (e.g. CU_NAVY, CU_RED) are importable directly and may be used wherever a Matplotlib colour argument is accepted. N-aware colour selection The core design principle is that the right colours for a figure depend on how many series are being plotted. get_palette(n) returns a curated list of exactly n colours following a consistent sequencing logic: n = 2 primary blue + primary red n = 3 + soft grey (neutral third) n = 4 full blue pair then full red pair n = 5-6 bb rr + grey shades as fillers n = 7+ grey drops out; chromatic families expand in order n = 13-20 curated n=12 sequence extended with neutrals and darks n > 20 full palette cycled The intent is that similar colours cluster together: a stacked area chart with four series will show two blues and two reds, which read as two distinct groups rather than four unrelated hues. Legend placement style_legend(ax, n=n) applies consistent legend formatting and automatically places the legend outside the axes for n >= 4, where an in-axes legend would typically occlude data. Both behaviours can be overridden explicitly. Always call fig.tight_layout() afterwards when placing outside. Colormaps Two named Matplotlib colormaps are provided for continuous data: CU_DIVERGING navy -> white -> red; for variables with a meaningful zero (correlations, residuals, z-scores). CU_SEQUENTIAL white -> navy; for one-directional variables such as counts, densities, or probabilities. Both are registered with Matplotlib on import and can be passed directly to any cmap= argument. Axis utilities set_yaxis_thousands(ax) and set_xaxis_thousands(ax) format tick labels with comma separators (e.g. 1500000 -> 1,500,000). annotate_bars(ax) adds value labels to bar charts automatically, handling both vertical and horizontal orientations. despine(ax) removes the top and right spines for a cleaner look, suitable for presentations or blog posts. Time series utilities add_vspans(ax, periods) shades a list of (start, end) periods as semi-transparent vertical bands — useful for marking recessions, wars, or other historical episodes on time series plots. add_vlines(ax, events) draws vertical lines at point-in-time events such as elections, crashes, or policy announcements. Supports optional text labels and partial vertical extent via ymin / ymax . Saving for LaTeX save_for_latex(fig, name) writes PDF and PNG to a figures/ directory. By default it strips Matplotlib titles before saving so that LaTeX can supply captions via \caption{} with proper typography and \label{} cross-reference support; titles are restored in memory afterwards. Pass split_panels=True to additionally save each subplot individually, suitable for the LaTeX subcaption environment. 1050 1051 1052 1053 1054 1055 1056 1057 1058 1059 1060 """ th_style — Academic Matplotlib Style ====================================== A personal, reusable Matplotlib configuration module built around the Charles University (Karlova Univerzita) official colour palette, extended with complementary colour families for multi-series academic figures. Colour palette -------------- The palette is organised into seven chromatic families — blues, reds, yellows, greens, oranges, purples — plus a range of neutrals and fill greys. All named constants (e.g. CU_NAVY, CU_RED) are importable directly and may be used wherever a Matplotlib colour argument is accepted. N-aware colour selection ------------------------ The core design principle is that the right colours for a figure depend on how many series are being plotted. ``get_palette(n)`` returns a curated list of exactly ``n`` colours following a consistent sequencing logic: - n = 2 primary blue + primary red - n = 3 + soft grey (neutral third) - n = 4 full blue pair then full red pair - n = 5-6 bb rr + grey shades as fillers - n = 7+ grey drops out; chromatic families expand in order - n = 13-20 curated n=12 sequence extended with neutrals and darks - n > 20 full palette cycled The intent is that similar colours cluster together: a stacked area chart with four series will show two blues and two reds, which read as two distinct groups rather than four unrelated hues. Legend placement ---------------- ``style_legend(ax, n=n)`` applies consistent legend formatting and automatically places the legend outside the axes for n >= 4, where an in-axes legend would typically occlude data. Both behaviours can be overridden explicitly. Always call ``fig.tight_layout()`` afterwards when placing outside. Colormaps --------- Two named Matplotlib colormaps are provided for continuous data: ``CU_DIVERGING`` navy -> white -> red; for variables with a meaningful zero (correlations, residuals, z-scores). ``CU_SEQUENTIAL`` white -> navy; for one-directional variables such as counts, densities, or probabilities. Both are registered with Matplotlib on import and can be passed directly to any ``cmap=`` argument. Axis utilities -------------- ``set_yaxis_thousands(ax)`` and ``set_xaxis_thousands(ax)`` format tick labels with comma separators (e.g. 1500000 -> 1,500,000). ``annotate_bars(ax)`` adds value labels to bar charts automatically, handling both vertical and horizontal orientations. ``despine(ax)`` removes the top and right spines for a cleaner look, suitable for presentations or blog posts. Time series utilities --------------------- ``add_vspans(ax, periods)`` shades a list of (start, end) periods as semi-transparent vertical bands — useful for marking recessions, wars, or other historical episodes on time series plots. ``add_vlines(ax, events)`` draws vertical lines at point-in-time events such as elections, crashes, or policy announcements. Supports optional text labels and partial vertical extent via ``ymin``/``ymax``. Saving for LaTeX ---------------- ``save_for_latex(fig, name)`` writes PDF and PNG to a ``figures/`` directory. By default it strips Matplotlib titles before saving so that LaTeX can supply captions via ``\\caption{}`` with proper typography and ``\\label{}`` cross-reference support; titles are restored in memory afterwards. Pass ``split_panels=True`` to additionally save each subplot individually, suitable for the LaTeX ``subcaption`` environment. =============================================================================== The Vojenský historický archiv publishes name-level inventories of three wartime military courts in the Czech lands as born-digital PDFs (fetched by ``utils/scraping/fetch_vua_courts.py`` into ``data/raw/vua_courts/``): dg_praha Divizní soud Praha NAD 229, pomůcka č. 699 (2024) ldg_praha Zeměbranecký divizní soud Praha NAD 360, pomůcka č. 729 (2025) ldg_brno Zeměbranecký divizní soud – expozitura Brno NAD 356, pomůcka č. 704 (2024) Each case file is one entry:: 2 2//7 14 1/11 level, reference, running no., carton původní signatura: Dst 99/15 RŮŽIČKA Čabo (pěšák, c. a k. pěší pluk č. 35, nar. 1886). 1915 Stručný popis trestného činu: odešel 11. 1. 1915 z posádky bez ohlášení. Po dezerci následovaly krádeže. Obžalovací spis i rozsudek. obecný pojem: dezerce (delikt); krádeže odkazy na příbuzné dokumenty, archiválie a pomůcky (text): § 183 Militär-Strafgesetzbuch This module turns that into two tables: one row per **entry** (case file) and one row per **accused** — an entry can name a dozen people. What the text layer does, and how it is handled ----------------------------------------------- * The *Datace* column is a separate table cell; pdfplumber appends it to the **first line of the accused block** (``… pěší pluk č. 88, nar. 1914`` / ``1891).`` — the 1914 is the date of the file, not a birth year). It is cut off that line by :data:`_DATACE`, which only matches 1910–1929, so a birth year can never be taken for it. * Every page repeats two header lines and ends in its page number. A numeric line is dropped only when a page header follows it, so a wrapped line that happens to be a bare number survives. * A file kept in several cartons has no carton of its own; its parts follow as level-3 rows (``3 4//86/1 1128 104`` / ``1. část spisu 1918``) and their cartons are collected. * The description and the note on what the file holds share one cell. The note opens with one of a handful of formulas (*Obžalovací spis…*, *Šetření ukončeno…*, *Spisy bez rozsudku…*, *Řízení…*, *Rozsudek…*); ``outcome_text`` starts at the first such line. What the source does not say ---------------------------- * **Brno lists places without labelling them** (``civilní osoba, Vlkoš, Kyjov, nar. 1893``). The first is read as the birthplace and the rest as the domicile; where the inventory is explicit (``Bialystok (Polsko), přísl. Brno``) that reading holds, but it is inferred. ``birthplace_how`` records which side of ``nar.`` the place stood on. * **Unauthorised absence has no subject term.** ``absence`` is § 212 of the *Militär-Strafgesetzbuch* **or** the wording of the description (:data:`_ABSENCE_TEXT`: *svévolně se vzdálit od svého útvaru*, *překročit povolenou dovolenku* …). That § 212 is *eigenmächtige Entfernung* is read off the inventories themselves — it is the paragraph cited where a description says "bez úmyslu dezerce" — and has **not** been checked against the text of the 1855 code; check it before the flag carries a result. The two components are kept apart in ``absence_par212`` / ``absence_text``. ``work_absence`` is a different thing: the subject term for militarised labourers who left a mine or a works. * **Desertion** is the subject term ``dezerce (delikt)`` **or** § 183 of the military code, again with both components kept (``desertion_term`` / ``desertion_par183``). * Survival is partial: the 1917–18 files were heavily weeded (DG Praha lost roughly two thirds), and these are hinterland courts — men caught at home, not men who crossed the lines.
